We prove that if $G$ has minimum degree at least $d$ and each edge belongs to at most $d/k^2$ triangles, where $k=\lfloor\log d/\log\log d\rfloor$, then $G$ contains an induced bipartite subgraph of average degree $Ω(\log d/\log\log d)$.

items.title: Paper2Lean: Agentic Autoformalization of Mathematical Research Papers at Scale
items.summary: Formalizing a mathematical research paper requires more than translating isolated theorems: statements and proofs must remain semantically faithful to the source and globally consistent across long-range dependencies. We introduce Paper2Lean, an end-to-end agentic framework that converts mathematical research papers into integrated Lean projects. The framework extracts mathematical content into a dependency graph and coordinates specialized agents for statement formalization, semantic checking and repair, proof construction, and project integration. We evaluate Paper2Lean on 20 mathematical optimization research papers, using mathlib and a shared library of supporting results. All 20 automatically generated projects compile successfully without proof placeholders. Following human review and semantic repair, we introduce OptPaper-20, a corpus of 20 corrected paper-level formalizations comprising 494 Lean files and 110,910 lines of Lean code. All released projects pass clean builds, with no unresolved discrepancies identified in the audit. These results demonstrate the feasibility of agentic paper-level formalization while highlighting semantic fidelity as a central challenge beyond proof verification. The source code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/TTony2019/OptPaper

items.title: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture
items.summary: We show that any area-preserving $C^r$-diffeomorphism of a two-dimensional surface displaying an elliptic fixed point can be $C^r$-perturbed to one exhibiting a chaotic island whose metric entropy is positive, for every $1\le r\le \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Herman stating that the identity map of the disk can be $C^\infty$-perturbed to a conservative diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy. This implies also that the Chirikov standard map for large and small parameter values can be $C^\infty$-approximated by a conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy (a weak version of Sinai's positive metric entropy conjecture). Finally, this sheds light onto a Herman's question on the density of $C^r$-conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy: we show the existence of a dense set formed by conservative diffeomorphism which either are weakly stable (so, conjecturally, uniformly hyperbolic) or display a chaotic island of positive metric entropy.

items.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of a Class of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
items.summary: We prove local smoothing estimates for a class of Schrödinger operators on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

items.title: Oscillatory integral operators of arbitrary signature: beyond the universal estimates
items.summary: We consider Hörmander oscillatory integral operators on $\mathbb{R}^n$. In particular, we are interested in proving bounds with dependence on the signature of the phase. The sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^p$ estimates was obtained for any given signature by the second author and Iliopoulou. Under the mild non-compression hypotheses on the phase introduced in Chen et al., we prove $L^p\to L^p$ estimates that go beyond this universal range in odd dimensions. We also obtain the sharp universal range of $L^p\to L^q$ estimates for odd $n$. The techniques are based on the breakthrough work of Wang--Wu on the Fourier restriction conjecture.

items.title: An asymptotic bound for Yuster's independent transversal factor conjecture
items.summary: An $[r,n,1]$-graph has $r$ independent parts of size $n$, with a matching between each pair of parts. Yuster conjectured in 2021 that every such graph has a partition into independent transversals whenever $n\ge 2\lceil r/2\rceil$. We prove that there is an absolute constant $A>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $r$, this partition exists whenever $n\ge\lceil r+A r^{20/21}\rceil$. Thus $f(r)\le r+O(r^{20/21})$, where $f(r)$ is the least $n_0$ such that every $[r,n,1]$-graph has such a partition whenever $n\ge n_0$. In particular, $f(r)/r\to1$, giving an asymptotic form of the conjecture.

items.title: Combinatorial Dvoretzky Theory
items.summary: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional polytope such that $P \subset B_2^n$. Let $M^*(P)$ denote its mean width, and let $N$ be the number of facets (faces of dimension $n-1$) of $P$. We prove the following two bounds: (1) If $N \leq e^n$, then \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{\log^2(\frac{N}{n})}. \] (2) For arbitrary $N$, \[ M^*(P) \leq 1 - \frac{c}{n}N^{-\frac{2}{n-1}}. \] In both bounds, $c>0$ is an absolute constant.

items.title: Global-in-time maximal regularity for the Dunkl heat equation in BMO
items.summary: We establish global-in-time maximal regularity for the Cauchy problem of the Dunkl heat equation in BMO, without assuming reflection invariance of the external force. For a Hilbert-valued BMO function $F$, we integrate the spatial mean-square oscillation of the Dunkl gradient of its heat extension over all $t>0$ on each fixed Euclidean ball. The supremum of these integrals is comparable to the squared BMO seminorm of $F$. In particular, the upper estimates imply time-weighted energy estimates for the zero-initial-value solution and maximal regularity for nonzero initial values whose weak Dunkl derivatives belong to BMO.

items.title: Presentations of the cohomology ring of Hessenberg varieties for the minimal nilpotent orbit in type A
items.summary: In 2016 Abe and Crooks found a presentation for the cohomology ring of Hessenberg varieties associated with the minimal nilpotent orbit. Specifically, they presented the ring as a quotient of the cohomology ring of the flag variety, and described the kernel of the quotient map as the span of certain Schubert classes. This note improves upon their result in the Lie type A case, by giving a minimal generating set for the kernel. Our description uses substantially fewer generators than that of Abe-Crooks. Our list consists of a set of Schubert polynomials associated to permutations constructed from the Hessenberg function ${\mathbf h}$.

items.title: A non-zero gap for the planar Mumford-Shah convex lifting and the nonexistence of crack-tip calibrations
items.summary: We prove that the convex lifting of the Mumford-Shah functional constructed through the notion of calibration introduced in [2] is not sharp in dimension two. For Dirichlet boundary data prescribed by the crack-tip function, we construct a lifted competitor whose energy is strictly lower than that of the crack-tip subgraph. Since the crack-tip minimizes the original Mumford-Shah functional, this establishes a strict gap between the infima of the original and lifted problems. As a consequence we establish that the crack-tip admits no calibration.

items.title: Infinite graphs with finite metric dimension
items.summary: We study the metric dimension (strong and weak) of connected infinite graphs. In particular, our main interest is characterizing infinite graphs with finite dimension. Our main results: (1) graphs with more than one end have infinite strong dimension; (2) for locally finite graphs with a finite number of cycles, the weak dimension is finite if and only if the graph has finitely many vertices of degree at least three, and the strong dimension is finite if and only if the graph has one end and finitely many vertices of degree at least three.

items.title: Invariance and Expressiveness: Modal Variations
items.summary: This contribution focuses on bisimulation invariance as the hallmark of modal model theory and of modal modelling. It exemplifies traditional as well as more recent ramifications \&\ extensions of classical results -- involving variant modes of bisimulation equivalence and matching modalities also beyond plain Kripke structures, and emphasising especially the technical challenges in finite model theory and other non-elementary settings. Main results to be discussed revolve about the theme of expressive completeness phenomena: beside expressive completeness under bisimulation invariance in relation to first-order background logics, in the style of van Benthem--Rosen characterisations, this also concerns maximality results under criteria form abstract model theory, in the style of Lindstroem theorems.

items.title: Oddomorphisms, Split-Off Minors, and the Strong Roberson Conjecture
items.summary: We show that the existence of an oddomorphism from a graph $F$ to a graph $G$ does not imply that $G$ is a minor of $F$. This answers a question posed by Roberson (2026) and shows that the CFI graphs cannot be used to prove the Strong Roberson Conjecture. Additionally, we introduce the concept of a split-off minor and show that the existence of an oddomorphism from $F$ to $G$ implies that $G$ is a split-off minor of $F$. Consequently, every class that is closed under taking split-off minors and disjoint unions is homomorphism distinguishing closed. The split-off minor relation is the first minor-like structural relation shown to have this property, marking a meaningful advancement in our understanding of the interaction between structural graph containment and homomorphism indistinguishability relations.

items.title: Locally eventually onto cellular automata
items.summary: We give a new checkable criterion to ensure that a one-dimensional cellular automaton on a finite alphabet is open and locally eventually onto. In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be open and locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention. Building on Sutner's work with de Bruijn graphs, we describe a method for deciding openness and at the same time determining n. We then introduce the notion of block-regularity of local rules as a generalization of bipermutivity and prove that it implies openness. We further identify two conditions that, together with block-regularity, ensure that every nonempty cylinder set is mapped onto the whole configuration space after a finite number of iterations, and hence that the cellular automaton is open and locally eventually onto. The appendix provides the algorithms that check these finite criteria and then presents examples of open, locally eventually onto, non-bipermutive cellular automata for small diameters.

items.title: Nonabelian mirrors and Gromov-Witten invariants
items.summary: We propose quantum differential equations (QDEs) for periods of nonabelian mirror theories and develop an algorithm for constructing them directly from the mirrors. We verify the proposal by recovering known quantum differential equations of Grassmannians and Picard-Fuchs equations of Calabi-Yau complete intersections in Grassmannians. Our algorithm applies to a broad class of nonabelian GLSMs and yields new examples of quantum differential equations for several Fano varieties. The associated cohomology-valued generating functions can be extracted directly from these equations. Using them, we compute instanton numbers of both complete-intersection and non-complete-intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds, including the Pfaffian and Gulliksen--Negård Calabi-Yau threefolds. The resulting instanton numbers agree with all previously known computations, while the generating functions obtained for the non-complete-intersection examples are new.

items.title: A note on Guo's perturbation result for symmetric nonnegative matrices
items.summary: In 1997 Guo Wuwen proved that if $(λ_1,λ_2,\dots,λ_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix with Perron eigenvalue $λ_1$ and $λ_2$ real, then $(λ_1+t,λ_2\pm t,λ_3,\dots,λ_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix for every $t\ge 0$. Whether the same holds for symmetric nonnegative matrices has remained an open question. We give an affirmative answer, in a slightly stronger form: if $A$ is a symmetric nonnegative matrix with Perron eigenvalue $λ_1$ and further eigenvalues $λ_2,\dots,λ_n$, and $d_1\ge|d_2|+\dots+|d_n|$, then there is a symmetric matrix $B\ge A$ with eigenvalues $λ_1+d_1,\dots,λ_n+d_n$, and $B$ has the same diagonal as $A$ when $d_1+\dots+d_n=0$. This leads us to call a symmetrically realizable list \emph{Guo-extreme} if none of Guo's moves can be reversed for this list. Every symmetrically realizable list is a Guo-extreme list plus a vector from the cone of Guo's moves. Our second main result is a certificate, modeled on a theorem of Laffey on extreme symmetric matrices: if every nonnegative symmetric matrix that commutes with $A$ and is equal to zero on the entries where $A$ is positive is a multiple of the identity, then $A$ is orthogonally similar to a positive matrix if $A$ has a positive diagonal entry, and to a matrix with zero diagonal and positive off-diagonal entries if $A$ has zero diagonal. Consequently, the spectrum of $A$ can be moved by a small amount in every direction, respectively in every trace-preserving direction, and remain symmetrically realizable. In particular, the spectrum of such a matrix is not Guo-extreme.

items.title: A type theory for invertibility in weak $ω$-categories
items.summary: We present a conservative extension ICaTT of the dependent type theory Catt for weak $ω$-categories with a type witnessing coinductive invertibility of cells. This extension allows for a concise description of the ``walking equivalence'' as a context, and of a set of maps characterising $ω$-equifibrations as substitutions. We provide an implementation of our theory, which we use to formalise basic properties of invertible cells. These properties allow us to give semantics of ICaTT in marked weak $ω$-categories, building a fibrant marked $ω$-category out of every model of ICaTT.

items.title: Regularity of the Semigroup of Regular Probability Measures on Locally Compact Hausdorff Topological Groups in which every element is of finite order
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group in which every element is of finite order, and let $P(\mathcal{G})$ denote the class of all regular probability measures on $\mathcal{G}$. In this note, it is observed that a characterization of algebraically regular elements in certain subsemigroups of $P(\mathcal{G})$ (Theorem~4.1 \cite{MNN}) for compact $\mathcal{G}$ remains true for locally compact $\mathcal{G}$. The results presented rely very much on Wendel's support theorem and the theory of doubly stochastic matrices (\cite{PLC} \cite{WEN}). A more general situation in which the assumption that every element is of finite order is not satisfied is also considered and illustrated with an example. This short article is a followup of \cite{MNN}.In addition,the random walk on an infinite discrete group associated with the generalised inverse of a probability measure is also studied.The last section is devoted to Fourier transform techniques to study the same problem using Bochner-type theorem in harmonic analysis.

items.title: Variational analysis of determinantal varieties
items.summary: Determinantal varieties---the sets of bounded-rank matrices or tensors---have attracted growing interest in low-rank optimization. The tangent cone to low-rank sets is widely studied and underpins a range of geometric methods. The second-order geometry, which encodes curvature information, is more intricate. In this work, we develop a unified framework to derive explicit formulas for both first- and second-order tangent sets to various low-rank sets, including low-rank matrices, tensors, symmetric matrices, and positive semidefinite matrices. The framework also accommodates the intersection of a low-rank set and another set satisfying some assumptions, thereby yielding a tangent intersection rule. Through the lens of tangent sets, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition under which a nonsmooth problem and its smooth parameterization share equivalent second-order stationary points. As applications, we exploit tangent sets to characterize optimality conditions for low-rank optimization and prove that verifying second-order optimality is NP-hard. Moreover, for low-rank semidefinite programs, the Burer--Monteiro parameterization maps fourth-order stationary points of the parameterized problem to second-order stationary points of the original problem. In a separate line of analysis, we investigate variational geometry of the graph of the normal cone to matrix varieties, deriving the explicit Bouligand tangent cone, Fréchet and Mordukhovich normal cones to the graph. These results are further applied to develop optimality conditions for low-rank bilevel programs.

items.title: Matrix-point interpolation for positive real odd functions in one and several variables
items.summary: We study the single matrix point interpolation problem for positive real matrix valued functions on the right half-plane, both in the single variable setting and in the noncommutative multivariable setting. In the single variable case, a careful analysis is done for when the solution may or must have a pole at infinity. In the multivariable setting, as the pole structure at infinity can be more complicated, we focus on the case when there is no pole at infinity. The results also yield numerical algorithms for finding a solution.

items.title: A Formalism for Merging Power Series in Solving Multinomial Equations: Master Series and Master Numbers
items.summary: It is shown that all solutions of the canonical equation y^a = 1 + a*x*y^b with arbitrary complex exponents a, b (case m = 1) and of its limiting cases - the binomial root y = (1 + a*x)^(1/a) at b = 0, the exponential y = e^x at a = 0, b = 0, and the Lambert equation y = e^(x*y^b) at a = 0 - as well as the logarithms of these solutions (case m = 0), are expressed by a single power master series M(m; a; b; x) = m + x + ((m - a + 2b)/2!) x^2 + ((m - a + 3b)(m - 2a + 3b)/3!) x^3 + ... For multivalued solutions beyond the radius of convergence, a geometric criterion for selecting the conjugate series (the same master series, but with a different set of parameters M(m; a'; b'; x')) is proposed, ensuring branch continuity on the complex plane. This representation of power series in terms of master numbers not only allows one to compute coefficients in degenerate cases where the gamma-function representation loses meaning, but also provides a transparent analytical algorithm for the merge operation on master series. The method is illustrated on problems in gas dynamics and plasma physics, where it is demonstrated that physically realizable states require the application of conjugate series beyond the radius of convergence of the basic expansion.

items.title: Willmore stability of minimal surfaces in the n-sphere
items.summary: We prove that the Lawson minimal surface $ξ_{g,1}$ in $S^3$ is strongly stable for the Willmore bending energy $W$ and remains strongly $W$-stable in $S^n$ for every $n \geq4$; our proof starts with a new lower bound on the area-index of $ξ_{m,k}$ for $m\geq k>1$. Next we observe that each of the $ξ_{m,k}$ and the Karcher-Pinkall-Sterling minimal surfaces in $S^3$, as well as the equilateral minimal torus in $S^5$, is the unique $W$-minimizer in its conformal class, up to Möbius transformations of $S^n$. Finally, we show that although the equilateral minimal torus is $W$-stable in $S^n$ for every $n \geq5$, it is neither strongly $W$-stable nor a local $W$-minimizer: it has a 2-dimensional space of $W$-Jacobi fields on which almost everywhere the third-variation of $W$ is nonzero.

items.title: Concentration of plane branches: building a complete equisingularity invariant
items.summary: We study the concentration of the semigroup of values of a plane algebroid branch over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic. We give an explicit formula for it in terms of the multiplicities of the branch and of its strict transform; in particular, it is an invariant of the equisingularity class. Applying it to the successive strict transforms, we associate a concentration sequence with each branch. This sequence is not a complete equisingularity invariant: we describe all the multiplicity sequences sharing a given concentration sequence, give an algorithm to compute them, and count them in terms of certain positions of the sequence, which we call free. We also characterize the sequences of positive integers that arise as concentration sequences. Finally, we build a complete equisingularity invariant: the concentration sequence, together with the conductor of the semigroup of values, determines the equisingularity class of the branch, while neither of them does so alone. In characteristic zero, this means that the concentration sequence and the Milnor number form a complete invariant.

items.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
items.summary: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)$ is the $ρ(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $Π(ρ)$ under Scholze's functor, and $Π(ρ)$ is the representation associated to $ρ$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

items.title: Mixing Regularization for Average-Reward $Q$-Learning and $Q$-Planning
items.summary: The average-reward setting for reinforcement learning is challenging because, without discounting, the span-contraction of the Bellman operator depends on the mixing properties of the underlying Markov dynamics. Whereas existing work typically assumes contraction, for instance through environment mixing, we study regularization toward a given reward-agnostic, $m$-step mixing policy to control the mixing properties of the learned policy. Our central mixing lemma quantifies how the reference policy's mixing properties transfer to the resulting learned policies. In particular, a single regularizer-dependent quantity simultaneously controls the contraction of the regularized Bellman operator and the exploration of the resulting policies. A second regularizer-dependent quantity controls the bias introduced by regularization, revealing a trade-off between convergence speed and approximation accuracy. Building on this result, we establish finite-time guarantees for regularized $Q$-iteration, synchronous and single-trajectory $Q$-learning, and $Q$-planning. Under one-step mixing, our bounds for approximating the regularized fixed point match the classical model-query bound for relative value iteration and, up to logarithmic factors, an existing sample-complexity bound for synchronous $Q$-learning. We also establish finite-time guarantees under multi-step mixing. For $Q$-planning, we characterize how the planning horizon trades off boundary bias against sample complexity. Finally, we present numerical studies validating the analysis: (i) knowledge of a strong mixing policy improves convergence and exploration, with larger benefits under more severe bottlenecks; and (ii) the observed rankings of $α$-divergence regularizers by bias and convergence speed are consistent with our theoretical analysis.

items.title: Fröberg's Conjecture for Products of Linear Forms: Split Powers and Inherited Syzygies
items.summary: Fröberg's conjecture predicts the Hilbert series of a polynomial ring modulo general forms. We study explicit products of linear forms over fields of characteristic zero. In four variables, six $d$th powers fail to attain the predicted series for $d\ge4$. We fix seven rational directions, take five $d$th powers, and split the sixth generator between the two remaining directions with exponents $\lceil d/2\rceil$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$. The quotient has the predicted series for $1\le d\le30$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $d$, its Hilbert function agrees with the prediction in every degree $q\le(11/5-\varepsilon)d$ or $q\ge(73/32+\varepsilon)d$. In contrast, for $d\ge4$ the predicted series cannot occur if each of the six forms has a linear factor of multiplicity at least $(15d+91)/16$. In three variables, relations among five powers $L_i^e$ give relations among the products $L_i^eM_i$. For five general pairs of linear forms and $e\ge36$, these relations and the pure-power Hilbert function give a lower bound whose error is at most $55$ in every degree and is zero through degree $\lfloor(7e+5)/4\rfloor-2$. The maximum excess over the comparison proposed by Shapiro is $(10/3)e+O(\sqrt e)$.

items.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
items.summary: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $Δ^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[ c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}. \] The second equality confirms a conjecture of Bukh, Matoušek, and Nivasch, who established the upper bound. The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions of the author.

items.title: The one-shot problem: Solution to an open question of finite-fuel singular control with discretionary stopping
items.summary: We resolve a long-standing open question posed by Karatzas, Ocone, Wang, and Zervos (Stochastics, 2000) on finite-fuel singular stochastic control with discretionary stopping. Our approach introduces a novel "one-shot" solution technique, based on reduction to an auxiliary optimal stopping problem. We prove that, despite the convexity of the objective function, the waiting region of the optimal strategy need not be connected. Furthermore, we identify a qualitative transition in the optimal policy: even with arbitrarily small positive fuel, the solution can differ from the zero-fuel (pure optimal stopping) limit. These results reveal a fundamental non-robustness in such control problems, showing that zero-fuel models need not approximate behaviour under small but positive fuel constraints.

items.title: The existence of generalized Steiner systems
items.summary: A generalized Steiner system $GS(t,w,n,q)$ is a $q$-ary constant-weight code of length $n$ and weight $w$ that has minimum distance at least $2(w-t)+1$ and attains the Johnson-type upper bound $(q-1)^t\binom nt/\binom wt$. For strengths $t=1$ and $t=2$, such systems were known to exist for all sufficiently large lengths satisfying the necessary divisibility conditions. For general fixed parameters, Liu and Shangguan (J. Combin.\ Theory Ser.~A 209 (2025), 105955) proved that the Johnson-type bound is attained asymptotically, and asked whether it is attained with equality for all sufficiently large lengths satisfying these conditions. We answer this question affirmatively. We prove that, for fixed integers $q\geq3$ and $w>t\geq1$, a $GS(t,w,n,q)$ exists for every sufficiently large $n$ such that $\binom{w-i}{t-i}$ divides $(q-1)^{t-i}\binom{n-i}{t-i}$ for all $0\leq i<t$. Moreover, the system can be chosen so that the supports of distinct codewords intersect in at most $t$ coordinates. Our proof assigns an independent random labelling to every set of $t+1$ coordinates, which turns large support intersections into conflicts in an exact covering problem, and then applies Keevash's decomposition theorem for labelled complexes.

items.title: Todd's relation conjecture and binary relations for multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
items.summary: We prove Todd's relation conjecture: all $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear relations of Thakur's multiple zeta values are generated from the fundamental binary relation by the operators $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}\circ \mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$; moreover they are also generated by $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}\circ\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$. The $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}$-part of this conjecture has been proved by Chang, Chen and Mishiba. We prove the whole conjecture for Carlitz multiple polylogarithm values, which implies the $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}$-part for multiple zeta values. We also determine all fixed relations and binary relations. Let $\mathfrak{BR}^{\mathrm{S}}_w$ be the $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear space spanned by binary relations of weight $w$, and let $\operatorname{Fix}^{\mathrm{S}}_w$ be the $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear space spanned by fixed relations. We derive generating functions $\sum_{w\ge 1}\bigl(\dim_{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}\operatorname{Fix}^{\mathrm{S}}_w\bigr)x^w=\frac{x^{q+1}(1-x)}{(1-2x)(1-2x+x^{q+1})}$ and $\sum_{w\ge 1}\bigl(\dim_{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}\mathfrak{BR}^{\mathrm{S}}_w\bigr)x^w=\frac{x^q(1-x)}{(1-2x)(1-2x+x^{q+1})}.$ Our results are based on the recent work of Im-Kim-Ngo Dac on the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations of Thakur's multiple zeta values, and a system of transfer theorems between multiple zeta values and multiple polylogarithm values.

items.title: Learning Multinomial Logits in $O(n \log n)$ time
items.summary: A Multinomial Logit (MNL) model is composed of a finite universe of items $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, each assigned a positive weight. A query specifies an admissible subset---called a slate---and the model chooses one item from that slate with probability proportional to its weight. This query model is also known as the Plackett--Luce model or conditional sampling oracle in the literature. Although MNLs have been studied extensively, a basic computational question remains open: given query access to slates, how efficiently can we learn weights so that, for every slate, the induced choice distribution is within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the ground truth? This question is central to MNL learning and has direct implications for modern recommender system interfaces. We provide both adaptive and non-adaptive algorithms for this task. Our first adaptive algorithm makes $O(\frac{n\log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ queries and learns every choice distribution in total variation distance $\varepsilon$. We also provide a second adaptive algorithm that with $O(\frac{n \log n}{\varepsilon^3})$ queries provides a stronger guarantee: each choice distribution is approximated to a multiplicative $1\pm\varepsilon$ error (except for subsets of mass smaller than $\varepsilon$). We complement these algorithms with lower bounds of $Ω(\frac{n\log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ for total variation distance and $Ω(\frac{n \log n}{\varepsilon^3})$ for the multiplicative error guarantee, showing the optimality of our adaptive algorithms. Our non-adaptive algorithm makes $O\left(\frac{n^{2}}{\varepsilon^{3}}\log n \log\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)$ queries to obtain guarantees under the multiplicative error notion. We complement this result with an $Ω(\frac{n^2 \log n}{\varepsilon^2})$ lower bound for any non-adaptive algorithm, showing that our algorithm is almost tight in $n$ (within a $\log n$ factor).

items.title: On the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
items.summary: This paper gives a new path to determine all $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic, which had been done by Huang, Lai, Li and the author. The path used in this paper is based on the idea of operator generation, which originated from the work of Todd, developed by the author, and independently by Im-Kim-Ngo Dac.

items.title: On the variation of slopes over moduli stacks of Galois representations
items.summary: In studying slopes of p-adic eigenforms, focusing on eigenforms with a fixed residual Galois representation is a standard approach. In this paper, we go further and explicitly study how slopes vary as the residual representations vary over a characteristic p space that is closely related to Emerton and Gee's moduli stack of Galois representations. This space, which was introduced in work of Dotto, Emerton, and Gee, is simply a chain of projective lines. We prove that as we move in one direction along this chain the slopes of eigenforms satisfy a snaking property: the n-th slope increases (resp. decreases) for n odd (resp. n even). Our method of proof involves first showing that another sequence of slopes, called the k-derivative slopes, follows its own snaking pattern over the moduli. This is quite interesting in its own right, as these slopes are closely related to slopes of L-invariants attached to eigenforms of level exactly divisible by p. As a consequence, we show that the authors' ghost conjecture, recently proven by Liu, Truong, Xiao, and Zhao, is "stable under direct sums". We determine how p-adic slopes of modular forms vary as their associated Galois representations modulo p vary over moduli of Galois representations. As a consequence, we show that the authors' ghost conjecture recently proven by Liu, Truong, Xiao, and Zhao is "stable under direct sums".

items.title: Surface sheaves on the quintic II. Donaldson-Thomas invariants and the M5-brane modified elliptic genus in string theory
items.summary: We compute Donaldson-Thomas invariants of pure two-dimensional sheaves in the hyperplane class of a smooth quintic threefold. We take advantage of two degenerating families to relate the DT geometry of Quintic threefold to geometry of pure two dimensional shaves on a quartic threefold and correction terms induced by invariants of relative Hilbert schemes of points. For this we use degeneration technique and virtual gluing formula in the prequel Part I. The marked virtual intersections, Chow specialization and complete moduli on the smooth quintic give nine coefficients of the M5-brane modified elliptic genus in string theory predicted by Gaiotto, Strominger and Yin, including its entire primitive polar part. Four geometric degrees determine the candidate in the prescribed modular space. We also construct a weight-26 period series on the complete hyperplane system and identify the contributions of twisted-cubic hulls and their point modifications on both sides.

items.title: How many sorted projections determine any n points in k dimensions?
items.summary: Let $d_1,\dots,d_m$ be directions in $\mathbb{R}^k$, where $k\ge 2$. A multiset $X$ of $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ projects to the $m$ multisets of numbers $\{\{x\cdot d_j : x\in X\}\}$, or equivalently to the $m$ sorted lists of these numbers. How many directions are needed for these projections to determine every multiset of $n$ points? Two simple bounds are known in every dimension: more than $(k-1)\log_2 n$ directions are always needed, and $(k-1)n+1$ directions in general position always suffice. In the plane much more is known: Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron showed that almost every choice of $O(\log n \log\log n)$ directions suffices. Whether anything similar holds in higher dimensions was left open by Dym, Wellershoff, Tsoukanis, Levy and Balan. We observe that two lemmas of Hair and Sahai, proved for list recovery of random linear codes, answer that question, and by tightening their argument we show that in every dimension almost every choice of $(4k-2)\ln(2n)\ln(k\log_2 2n)+k+1$ directions suffices. For $k\le 10$ this beats the linear bound once $n$ is larger than about 100: for example, 144 directions suffice for multisets of 1000 points in the plane, and an exact computation lowers this to 133. Letting some of the random blocks in their argument fail removes a factor $\log k$: almost every choice of $O(k\log n\log\log n)$ directions suffices, uniformly in $k$ and $n$. We also show that $2k-1$ directions never determine three points, so that the logarithmic lower bound is not tight; that every $m$ directions in the plane fail on some pair of multisets of size $O(1.65^m)$, improving the bound $O(1.80^m)$ of Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron; and that for each $k$, $m$ and $n$, either almost every choice of $m$ directions works or almost none does.

items.title: Equi-integrable approximation of Sobolev mappings between manifolds
items.summary: We show that limits of sequences of smooth maps between compact Riemannian manifolds with equi-integrable $W^{1, p}$-Sobolev energy can always be strongly approximated by smooth maps, giving a counterpart of Hang's density result in $W^{1, 1}$ for the Sobolev space $W^{1, p}$ with integer $p \ge 2$. Our result extends to higher-order Sobolev spaces and is straightforward in fractional Sobolev spaces. We also provide a proof based on the weak continuity of Jacobians in the cases where the cohomological criterion of Bethuel, Demengel, Colon and Hélein applies.

items.title: Surface sheaves on the quintic I. Expanded degenerations and virtual gluing
items.summary: We study the specialization of Donaldson-Thomas virtual cycles for surface sheaves on a Calabi Yau threefold degenerating to a simple normal crossing threefold, composed of two quasi Fano threefolds glued along a common (double) divisor. The compactification of the two relative sheaf moduli spaces involves construction of suitable moduli space of sheaves on expanded degenerations of each quasi Fano variety. On a fixed expanded fiber the matching datum is an equivalence of the derived restrictions of the component sheaves. We identify the corresponding deformation complexes and give valuative and obstruction-theoretic hypotheses under which the specialized virtual class is a sum over marked joining divisors. When a marked space is the full fiber product of proper relative factors over a smooth simple boundary moduli space, its class is a refined diagonal pullback. For the case of sheaves supported on hyperplane sections of the threefold we discuss construction of the proper relative family by descending the chartwise stable loci, and identify both marked pieces, including the one with zero boundary. To provide some examples, we carry out explicit constructions for the moduli space of surface structure sheaf and its twists. We also prove valuative results for specified sheaves with noninvertible hulls. In a sequel, Part II, we use the construction of degeneration technique in this article to compare quintic invariants with the predicted S-duality modularity of "M5-brane modified elliptic genus" provided by string theorists, Gaiotto Strominger and Yin.

items.title: The rigidity phenomenon for weighted composition operators on the Fock spaces
items.summary: We establish the rigidity of canonical sums of any finite number of weighted composition operators acting from a Fock space $\mathcal{F}^p$ into another $\mathcal{F}^q$ for all possible combinations of \(p,q\in (0, \infty]\). Specifically, we show that such a sum is bounded (compact, resp.) if and only if its summands are individually bounded (compact, resp.). In the case \(p\le q\), we present two independent approaches -- one analytic and one largely algebraic -- based on some common preliminary rigidity results. As a natural byproduct of our approach, we also obtain the Reproducing Kernel Thesis.

items.title: Convergence of the Most Probable Transition Paths in Multiscale Systems
items.summary: This paper is devoted to study the convergence behavior of the most probable transition paths in a class of multiscale stochastic dynamical systems. First, based on Euler-Lagrange equations, we establish proximity and convergence results in the space of continuous functions endowed with the supremum norm. These results compare the most probable paths of the multiscale system with those of averaged system derived from the averaging principle. Next, we utilize a variational framework and analyze the Onsager-Machlup functionals using $Γ$-convergence. Together with the equi-coercivity of the functional family, we prove the convergence of both their minima and minimizers. Specifically, we show weak convergence of the minimizers in the Cameron-Martin space $H^1$, which implies their strong convergence in $L^2$.

items.title: Uninorm constructions on bounded trellises via closure and interior operators
items.summary: In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which six closure- or interior-based operations on bounded trellises are uninorms. These operations incorporate triangular norms, triangular conorms, or both, and form three order-dual pairs. Since the underlying pseudo-order need not be transitive and meet and join need not be associative, standard lattice arguments do not apply directly. Under a fixed ambient transitivity assumption, the first pair is characterized by image, monotonicity, and compatibility conditions for the associated maps on elements incomparable with the neutral element; an additional comparison condition used in earlier sufficient constructions is shown to be redundant. Complete characterizations are also obtained for the variants with an absorbing endpoint, including both nondegenerate and degenerate interval cases. For the pair involving both a triangular norm and a triangular conorm, we derive exact comparison conditions requiring the triangular norm to take the value~$0$, or dually the triangular conorm to take the value~$1$, in the relevant cases. These conditions reduce to the usual incomparability assumptions in the absence of nontrivial zero- or one-divisors. On bounded lattices, the closure and interior conditions simplify to explicit identities or image restrictions. Finite proper-trellis examples clarify the role and limitations of the ambient transitivity assumptions.

items.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
items.summary: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element. Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, almost invariant color classes are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then show, via a separate argument for all slowly oscillating functions, that for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---Protasov's stronger conclusion holds: the full corona is a singleton.

items.title: Convex combinations of strict triangular norms
items.summary: We prove that a pointwise convex combination of two strict triangular norms with positive weights is associative if and only if the two norms coincide. Together with the known ordinal-sum reduction and nilpotent case, the theorem yields the same conclusion for all continuous triangular norms and, in particular, for associative bivariate copulas. It also gives a corresponding result for representable uninorms with a common neutral element.

items.title: Optimal Radius Ratio of Compact Nonuniform Packings
items.summary: We study the ratio of the smallest to the largest radius in a nonuniform disk packing whose tangency graph triangulates the plane. We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest possible ratio is $s=0.651050185882609\ldots$, attained uniquely up to similarity by packing~53 of Fernique, Hashemi, and Sizova. In fact, every nonuniform packing with radius ratio at least $0.65105$ is similar to this packing. No periodicity or restriction on the number of radii is assumed; the radii are required only to have a positive infimum and a finite supremum. Following the finite-subgraph exclusion program of Connelly and Zhang, we first restrict the degree-five flowers and their pairings. The remaining exceptional degree-seven corona forces seventeen complete flowers on an unfolded disk with thirty-seven labels. An exact interval certificate excludes their angle equations. A comparison of logarithmic radii on a recurrent network then forces the radii and the three local degree words. We identify the entire triangulation by reducing these words to the square--octagon tiling and showing that its decoration is forced.

items.title: Composition operators on weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc
items.summary: We study composition operators between weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc induced by smooth symbols. We prove a general result of continuity which only involves the behaviour of the symbol on the polytorus. We deduce from this several consequences about the automatic continuity of the induced operator. We study in depth the case of the tridisc and exhibit several examples showing that a characterization of continuity using only derivatives seems impossible.

items.title: Euler up-down numbers and quiver representations
items.summary: We show that Euler up-down numbers enumerate isoclasses of representations arising from quiver Grassmannians which provide an explicit realization of PBW degenerate flag varieties. Using this geometric realization, we derive several formulas connecting Euler up-down numbers, median Genocchi numbers, and Motzkin numbers. We also define a new $q$-analogue of Euler up-down numbers and derive several formulas for these polynomials. We describe a natural poset structure on the set of isoclasses of subrepresentations and describe it in terms of the classical degeneration order. Finally, we prove that the finer strata defined by fixing isotypes of sub- and quotient representations are the orbits under the automorphism group of the ambient quiver representation.

items.title: Invariant real curves arising from semiconjugacies of rational maps
items.summary: In this paper, we study real analytic invariant curves arising from semiconjugacies of real rational maps. Such semiconjugacies arise naturally in Eremenko's work on invariant Jordan analytic curves. While invariant generalized circles are easy to obtain from real rational maps, we are interested in curves not contained in any generalized circle. First, for a non-exceptional polynomial of degree at least two, we prove that every invariant curve arising from such a semiconjugacy is contained in a generalized circle. Second, in the rational map case, we construct invariant curves arising in this way that are not contained in any generalized circle and have arbitrarily many self-intersections, counted with multiplicity. Moreover, the rational maps can be chosen so that their restrictions to these curves have positive topological entropy.

items.title: Lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of expressible sets
items.summary: We obtain positive lower bounds on the Hausdorff dimension of sets of real numbers given by expressions of the form $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{a_n b_n}$, where $b_n$ satisfies some growth condition and $a_n$ lies in some set, possibly depending on $n$. As a consequence of our results, some of the irrational numbers arising from Erdős' celebrated construction from 1976 are not Liouville numbers.

items.title: Exact Differential Spectra for Five Families of Power Functions
items.summary: For a power function over a finite field, differential uniformity records only the largest entry of its differential distribution table, whereas the differential spectrum records every multiplicity and its frequency. We determine exact differential spectra for five families of low-uniformity power functions in odd characteristic, including families previously studied primarily through uniformity bounds. Our methods combine spectrum-preserving exponent changes, factorial moments, intersections of injective images, character sums, and point counts on curves over finite fields. For the ternary family of Yuan, Du, Qiao, and Zhou, we give a fixed-cover formula and an explicit Artin factorization for one pair-intersection cover; its odd-degree counts reduce to traces of elliptic and genus-two curves. Inverse-cubic powers yield a conic evaluation in characteristic five and low-genus trace formulas in larger characteristics. Four ternary branches associated with Dobbertin, Mills, Müller, Pott, and Willems share one complete spectrum governed by an elliptic trace. For the Yan--Han family, an Artin--Prym decomposition gives all multiplicity frequencies and exact differential uniformity, including a planar endpoint. For Felke's family, we express extension-field spectra as one-dimensional character sums while identifying the known prime-field cases. A standalone program independently reproduces the finite-field calculations used in the proofs.

items.title: On finiteness of fiber space structures of klt Calabi-Yau pairs in dimension 3
items.summary: We prove that for a fixed klt Calabi-Yau pair $(X,Δ)$ of dimension $3$, the set of fiber space structures of $X$ is finite up to $Aut(X,Δ)$.

items.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
items.summary: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. We disprove this conjecture for every exponent $n=2k$ with $k\ge3$ odd. For each such $n$, we prove that $D(C_n^r)>r(n-1)+1$ for every $r\ge 8n-7$.

items.title: Uniform Hypercontractivity and Log-Sobolev Inequality and Applications for Non-equilibrium Kinetic System
items.summary: In this paper, we derive exponential ergodicity in relative entropy for general kinetic SDEs under a partially dissipative condition. It covers non-equilibrium situations where the forces are not of gradient type and the invariant measure does not have an explicit density, extending previous results set in the equilibrium case. The key argument is to establish the hypercontractivity of the associated semigroup, which follows from its hyperboundedness and its $L^2$-exponential ergodicity. Moreover, we obtain exponential ergodicity in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance by combining Talagrand's inequality with a log-Harnack inequality. These results are further extended to the McKean-Vlasov setting and to the associated mean-field interacting particle systems under a suitable smallness condition on the distribution dependence. In the latter case, the convergence rates are uniform in the number of particles and we also establish the hypercontractivity and log-Sobolev inequality uniform in the number of particles using a new approach based on Girsanov's transform and hypercontractivity.

items.title: The FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research
items.summary: Operations research (OR) relies on algorithms that experts tailor to each problem: a new routing, scheduling or network design problem can take weeks of specialist work before it is solved well at scale. Large language model (LLM) agents now write, test and improve code, but whether they can design algorithms that scale to realistic instances is open: in the FrontierOR benchmark's one-shot evaluation, the strongest model matches Gurobi, with an objective within 1% of Gurobi's and no slower, on only 39% of the large instances. The FrontierOR Challenge asks teams to build agentic workflows that design, test, and improve algorithms for many optimization problems at once. Stage 1 releases 60 of the benchmark's 180 audited problems, spanning six application categories and five formulation types, in weekly rounds of 15; Stage 2 introduces new problems outside the benchmark, with unseen instances. Two tracks are ranked separately: in the Main track we run the submitted algorithms in a network-isolated sandbox with open-source dependencies only; in the Self-hosted track teams solve the instances on their own machines, with any software, within a timed window. Every solution is checked for feasibility, and a feasible solution scores the ratio of its objective to a frozen known reference, averaged over hidden instances.

items.title: Uniform Positivity of the $F$-Signature and Pure Descent of klt Singularities
items.summary: In this paper, we affirmatively answer the question of Carvajal-Rojas, Schwede, and Tucker on the uniform positivity of the $F$-signature, and prove a converse. Namely, given a klt type singularity, we establish uniform lower bounds on the $F$-signatures of its reductions mod $p$ for $p$ sufficiently large. Conversely, if the $F$-signatures of the reductions of a normal singularity are uniformly bounded below by a positive constant on large primes, we prove that the singularity is of klt type. As an application, we give a new reduction-mod-$p$ proof of Zhuang's theorem that klt type singularities descend along pure morphisms.

items.title: Beyond Robustness of Magic: Quantifying Quantum State Convertibility
items.summary: In fault-tolerant quantum computing, magic states provide essential resources for implementing non-Clifford operations. The robustness of magic (RoM) quantifies the magic contained in a quantum state and is closely related to the cost of classical simulation. However, knowing how much magic two states contain is not sufficient to determine whether one can be converted into the other using free operations. In this work, we develop a geometric framework in which RoM is represented as half the distance to the set of free states, and extend this framework to state conversion. We introduce a directed conversion deficiency that measures how far a target state lies from the states freely reachable from a given input. This quantity vanishes exactly when free conversion is possible and, beyond being a mathematically well-defined measure, has an operational interpretation in terms of stabilizer quasiprobability. Furthermore, our framework provides lower bounds on the additional magic states required for conversion that can be strictly stronger than conventional RoM-based bounds. We demonstrate this distinction analytically by constructing a continuous family of mixed single-qubit states with identical RoM for which free conversion is possible in one direction but impossible in the reverse. Our results reveal that the usefulness of magic for quantum state conversion depends not only on its amount but also on the specific transformation being performed.

items.title: Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
items.summary: We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$. In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.

items.title: The $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of perfectoid THH
items.summary: Let $R$ be a perfect $\mathbb F_p$-algebra or a nonzero $p$-torsionfree perfectoid ring and $p$ be an arbitrary prime number. We compute the $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of $\operatorname{THH}(R;\mathbb Z_p)$ for every $n\ge0$, including all homotopy groups, products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions and norms. We also compute genuine cyclotomic restriction.

items.title: Global-in-time L p -- L q estimates for solutions of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation
items.summary: In this work, we prove an optimal global-in-time $L^p \to L^q$ estimate for solutions to the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation with short range potential in dimension three. Our result shows that the decay rate as t $\rightarrow$ +$\infty$ is the same as the heat equation in x-variables and the divergence rate as t $\rightarrow$ 0 + is related to the sub-ellipticity with loss of 1/3 derivatives of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator.

items.title: Orbifold Chern slopes of surfaces with negative second Segre number and big cotangent bundle
items.summary: In this paper, we construct smooth minimal projective surfaces of general type with negative second Segre number and big cotangent bundle, and prove that every rational number in $(1,3]$ is realized as the orbifold Chern slope of a Du Val contraction of such a surface. The upper endpoint is attained by a canonical model with eighteen $A_8$ singularities and three $A_2$ singularities, which is a compact complex two-ball quotient by the equality case of the orbifold Miyaoka-Yau inequality. We also construct an explicit sequence of canonical-model orbifold Chern slopes converging to three from below. Our constructions are based on ramified base changes of semistable fibrations.

items.title: D-ripALM: A Tuning-friendly Decentralized Relative-Type Inexact Proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method
items.summary: This paper proposes D-ripALM, a Decentralized relative-type inexact proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method for consensus convex optimization over multi-agent networks. D-ripALM adopts a double-loop distributed optimization framework that accommodates a wide range of inner solvers, enabling efficient treatment of both smooth and nonsmooth objectives. D-ripALM employs a relative-type error criterion to regulate the switching between inner and outer iterations, replacing a prescribed absolute tolerance sequence with a single relative tolerance parameter. Moreover, we establish rigorous convergence guarantees for D-ripALM under general convexity assumptions, without requiring smoothness or strong convexity conditions commonly imposed in the distributed optimization literature. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that a restarted variant of D-ripALM achieves competitive computational efficiency and solution accuracy relative to representative decentralized algorithms.

items.title: Power topologies and uniformities on bistochastic operators
items.summary: We prove that the set of invertible Koopman operators attached to the usual interval probability space is dense (and hence dense $G_δ$) in the space of bistochastic operators in the polynomial weak topology. This extends the non-polynomial analogue (due to Brown/Vershik/Ryzhikov/Eisner). We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results.

items.title: Prime-Power Expansions and Boundary Corrections for the Secular Coefficients of Riemann-Zero Windows
items.summary: We study the secular coefficients of characteristic polynomials attached to finite windows of zeros of the Riemann zeta function, mapped onto the unit circle. Starting from the Riemann-von Mangoldt formula and Newton's identities, we derive a symmetric prime-power model for their generating function. The model carries an explicit boundary factor $(1-w)^{-ΔS}$, where $ΔS$ is the variation of $S(t)$ across the window. The boundary correction is determined by the integer zero count of the window rather than by a fitted parameter. For finite prime-power tails we prove a mean-square identity with an explicit diagonal term and an explicit error bound, using the Montgomery-Vaughan generalisation of Hilbert's inequality. Numerical experiments near $T = 10^6$, on computed but uncertified zeros, show that prime powers up to $Q = 32$, the zero count of the window and the known smooth term reproduce the secular coefficients. The median relative residual energy is $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ for $H = 181$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-5}$ for $H = 724$; the means are $2.1 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2.7 \times 10^{-3}$. The error is strongly asymmetric across windows. An exact convolution identity separates a residual, whose measured size does not depend on the boundary exponent, from its amplification by the boundary factor; the measured amplification follows the exponent over eight orders of magnitude. The diagonal prediction matches the measured power-sum residuals within 16% in the tested regimes. Exact identities and finite Dirichlet-polynomial estimates are kept separate from the numerical reconstruction. Extending the mean-square estimate to the true $S(t)$ is open and appears tied to pair correlations of zeros. This note does not propose a route to the Riemann hypothesis.

items.title: Sheetwise stationarity for stationary unions of $C^{1,α}$ graphs
items.summary: We prove that stationarity of a finite union of $C^{1,α}$ graphs implies stationarity of each individual graph, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. The proof closely follows the approach of Minter and Stanbury \cite{MinterStanbury}, who also raised this question in their Remark~1.6. As in their paper, we give a proof that uses the planar frequency results of Krummel, Minter and Wickramasekera \cite{KMW26} (but avoids the centre manifold construction of that paper). We also rely on the Schauder estimates for $Q$-valued functions established in \cite{Luc26}.

items.title: Refined Strichartz Estimates for sub-Laplacians in Heisenberg and $H$-type groups
items.summary: We obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the sub-Riemannian Schrödinger equation on $H$-type Carnot groups using Fourier restriction techniques. In particular, we extend the previously known Strichartz estimates previously obtained for the Heisenberg group also to non radial initial data. The same arguments permits to obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the wave equation on $H$-type groups. Our proof is based on estimates for the spectral projectors for sub-Laplacians and reinterprets Strichartz estimates as Fourier restriction theorems for nilpotent groups in the context of trace-class operator valued measures.

items.title: $C^{0}$ stability of torsion-free $G_{2}$ structures along the Laplacian flow
items.summary: In this paper, we prove that torsion-free $G_{2}$-structures are (weakly) dynamically stable along the Laplacian flow for closed $G_{2}$-structures in $C^{0}$-open neighbourhood. This weakens the assumption in \cite{LW19} and confirms Bryant's expectation \cite{Bry06} in the $C^{0}$ norm.

items.title: Information-Region MPC: Non-Iterative Distributed Control of Urban Traffic Signals
items.summary: Centralized model predictive control (MPC) exploits network-wide traffic information to obtain the optimal solution of the network-level control problem, but its computational burden grows rapidly with network size. Iterative distributed MPC reduces the size of local optimization problems, but requires repeated information exchange and coordination within each control update. To address these limitations, this paper proposes information-region MPC (IR-MPC), which approximates the first control input of centralized MPC using limited real-time data without iterative coordination. Based on historical traffic data, we quantify how perturbations at other intersections affect the centralized first control input of each intersection and use these couplings to construct a compact information region for every intersection. At each control update, each intersection then solves a local IR-MPC problem once using current data only from its information region. SUMO simulations on a real 28-intersection network show that IR-MPC with one processor per intersection computes its control inputs 9 times faster than centralized MPC and 15 times faster than a representative iterative decomposition-based distributed MPC method. IR-MPC reproduces 85% of the centralized control inputs exactly at the implemented one-second resolution, keeps 99.3% within 2s, and increases mean delay by only 0.03%.

items.title: Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game
items.summary: A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. This sweep is optimal against transit in both directions for $q\ge1/2$. At low speeds, $qW_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)/r$ tends to two, and an explicit ten-leg patrol guards width greater than $(2/q-1.235353)r$ throughout $0 < q\le1/40$. Rational spacetime and flux certificates give finite-speed bounds, including $6.944691333740r < W_{\mathrm{opt}}(1/4)\le8.10r$.

items.title: Perturbation Algorithm and Iterative Realization of a Four-Layer Semi-Discrete Scheme for an Evolutionary Problem with a Variable Operator
items.summary: In a Hilbert space, we consider the Cauchy problem for an evolutionary equation with the operator $A+B(t)$, where $A$ is a self-adjoint positive definite operator and $B(t)$ is a bounded operator depending on time. By means of the perturbation algorithm, the purely implicit four-layer semi-discrete scheme of the third order of approximation (the three-step backward differentiation formula) is reduced to three two-layer schemes, whose solutions are used to construct an approximate solution of the original problem. In each two-layer scheme, the term containing $B(t)$ is moved to the right-hand side, and the resulting equation is solved by an iterative method, so that only the time-independent operator $I+τA$ has to be inverted; the convergence of the iterations at the rate of a geometric progression with a ratio of order $τ$ is proved. A priori estimates for the two-layer and four-layer schemes are obtained by means of a discrete analogue of Gronwall's lemma. An estimate of order $τ^3$ for the error of the approximate solution is proved under an assumption on the difference quotients of the computed grid functions on the first layers. The results are illustrated by numerical experiments.

items.title: Maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs with given minimum degree and edge connectivity
items.summary: Let $G$ be a simple connected graph of order $n$ with minimum degree $δ$ and edge connectivity $k$. Recently, in [Linear Algebra Appl. 751 (2026) 318-330], Zhao, Ye, and Fan characterized the extremal graph with maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all graphs of order $n$ with minimum degree $δ$ and edge connectivity $k$ when $n \geq δ^2+4δ+3$ and $k \in \{0,1,2\}$, and proposed the corresponding problem for $3 \leq k \leq δ-1$. In this paper, we solve the problem for the entire range $0 \leq k \leq δ-1$ and completely remove the order restriction. Specifically, we prove that $$ q(G) \leq q(B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}), $$ with equality if and only if $G \cong B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}$, where $B_{n,n-δ-1}^{k}$ is the graph obtained from $K_{n-δ-1} \cup K_{δ+1}$ by adding $k$ edges joining a single vertex of $K_{n-δ-1}$ to $k$ distinct vertices of $K_{δ+1}$.

items.title: An almost effective proof of the class number 1 problem for imaginary quadratic fields via Frobenius--Rabinowitsch
items.summary: Let $D \neq 1$ be a square-free integer, and let $K = {\mathbb Q}(\sqrt D)$ be the corresponding quadratic field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ lying over an odd rational prime that splits in $K/\mathbb Q$. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition in terms of a binary quadratic form for $\mathcal{P}$ to be a principal ideal. Then, when $K$ is imaginary with $D\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ and $|D|>16$, we use this result to prove $K$ has class number 1 only if $D=1-4p$ where $p$, $4p-1$, and $4p+3$ are prime. Finally, combining this condition with results on the representation of integers by the sum of three squares, the theorem of Frobenius and Rabinowitsch, and a theorem of Tatuzawa we provide a proof, up to at most one possible additional field, of the well-known theorem on imaginary quadratic fields with class number 1. If Dirichlet $L$-functions have no zeros in the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>11/12$, then the possible additional field of our result does not exist.

items.title: Asymptotic efficiency comparison of explicit Dirichlet shape estimators
items.summary: In this study, we compare the asymptotic efficiency of three closed-form estimators of the Dirichlet shape parameters. We start by proving that, in the beta distribution, the score-adjusted moment estimator (SA) has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances than the usual moment estimator (M1) for both parameters. We then introduce a new moment estimator (M2) that combines the marginal moment equations to obtain a common estimate of the total concentration. M2 coincides with M1 in the beta case and has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances for every positive shape vector in three or more dimensions. We then show that SA is asymptotically more efficient than M2 when all shape parameters are equal; if at least two parameters differ, each estimator has smaller asymptotic variance than the other for some linear combination of the parameters. Furthermore, SA has strictly smaller componentwise asymptotic variances than M2 when all shape parameters are at least 1. Finally, we show that this ordering can reverse if a parameter becomes too small, and obtain relevant mathematical and computational bounds. Overall, the study shows that, for the Dirichlet distribution and under a broad range of parameter settings, score-adjusted estimation outperforms the classic moment estimation and identifies the limits of that advantage.

items.title: A New Look at the Classical Estimation Problem
items.summary: Bahadur's \emph{Lectures on the Theory of Estimation} develop the classical theory of point estimation inside the geometry of Hilbert space, and they record with unusual honesty where the theory strains: the locally best unbiased estimate depends on the parameter, a two-point parameter space yields an estimate Bahadur calls absurd, the odds in binomial sampling have no unbiased estimate, and the virtues of maximum likelihood remain heuristics. We present a subset of the lectures in Bahadur's notation and, at each strain, make one small modification: for each sample point, an estimate $τ$ becomes a function on the parameter space rather than a point in it. The result is the continuum of null hypotheses that Fisher, in 1955, identified with the theory of estimation; we call this \emph{generalized estimation}, and $τ$ a generalized estimator. Bahadur's own definition of an estimate, square-integrable at every distribution in the family, already supplies the domain. The payoffs are tracked lecture by lecture: estimators that exist at boundary samples where point estimates do not; an elementary lemma showing that no pointwise criterion admits a uniformly optimal estimator, which explains why admissibility, minimaxity, Bayes averaging and unbiasedness arose; assessment by information, $Λ(τ)$, with the score attaining the Fisher information bound uniformly by a three-line argument; Cramér--Rao attainment and sufficiency recovered as equality cases of that bound; and the maximum likelihood heuristics converted into exact statements about the score. Nothing classical is overturned; the classical apparatus is explained by Fisher's characterization of estimation as a continuum of significance tests.

items.title: On Gutt-Hutchings capacities of Minkowski sums and products of convex domains
items.summary: For Minkowski p-sums of convex domains, we establish Brunn-Minkowski-type inequalities for the full sequence of Gutt-Hutchings capacities. We also obtain explicitlower bounds for the Gutt-Hutchings capacities of Minkowski p-products. Our proof uses Matijevic's formula for Gutt-Hutchings capacities in terms of the Clarke dual-action functional and the Fadell-Rabinowitz index. By the equality of Gutt-Hutchings and Ekeland-Hofer capacities on star-shaped domains, the same inequalities hold for Ekeland-Hofer capacities.

items.title: Modeling sequential cognitive states via population level cortical dynamics
items.summary: In this work, we propose a mathematical framework for cyclic and sequential patterns of brain activity, combining heteroclinic dynamics with discrete neural-field models. Under explicit structural and positivity assumptions on the prescribed activity patterns, we show that the resulting spatially discrete neural-field system supports neither heteroclinic cycles nor nonconstant periodic orbits. Heteroclinic dynamics, on the other hand, arise in Lotka--Volterra-type systems, but these equations do not directly correspond to neuronal processes. To bridge these descriptions, we use a $C^1$ version of the Universal Approximation Theorem to approximate a target vector field by a neural network interpretable as a high-dimensional Amari-type neural-field system. Each periodic solution of the reduced dynamics admits a unique periodic realization at the population level with the same minimal period. For three-dimensional heteroclinic targets, we establish sufficient conditions ensuring that the approximating vector field admits a unique hyperbolic attracting periodic orbit in a trapping channel surrounding the original heteroclinic cycle. As a proof of concept, we apply this construction to a Lotka--Volterra-type target phenomenologically representing sequential network activations associated with focused-attention meditation.

items.title: Rational multisections and unirationality of supersingular K3 surfaces
items.summary: We prove that every supersingular K3 surface of Artin invariant at most nine is unirational, confirming the question of Artin, Rudakov, Shafarevich and Shioda outside the generic case of Artin invariant ten. In odd characteristic, we reduce the question to Artin invariant nine and sweep out the K3 surface by Abel--Jacobi images of rational multisections of its Artin--Tate twists which vary along the supersingular twistor line.

items.title: Multiple Positive Solutions of Minkowski-Curvature Neumann Problems with a Two-Step Indefinite Weight
items.summary: We study positive solutions of the Minkowski-curvature Neumann problem \[ \left(\frac{u'}{\sqrt{1-(u')^2}}\right)' + a(t)g(u)=0,\qquad u'(0)=u'(T)=0, \] with a two-step sign-changing weight. Under an explicit condition on an increasing nonlinearity \(g\), we prove that for every prescribed integer \(N\ge 1\) and every prescribed ratio \(κ>0\) of the step lengths, there exist step weights of that ratio and strictly negative integral for which the problem has at least \(N\) distinct positive solutions. The multiplicity persists under small perturbations of the weight parameters. A structural condition on \(g'/g\) yields at least three positive Neumann solutions for \(g(u)=e^{u^p}-1\) for every \(p>1\). An explicit increasing nonlinearity also satisfies the \(N\)-solution criterion for every finite \(N\), with the weight chosen separately in each case.

items.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank III: Lattice points of the Kozlov polytope
items.summary: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators and $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r Eg_i$ a graded free $E$-module with $°g_i=d_i$. Part I of this series identified the convex hull of the Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, $M$ a proper monomial submodule, as the Kozlov polytope $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$, a Minkowski sum of shifted Kozlov simplices, and described its vertices at rank two, conjecturing its facets there; Part II counted the Hilbert functions. Here we study the lattice points of the polytope. We show that the Kozlov simplex $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$ is a lecture hall simplex and that every point of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ has a unique chained decomposition into points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$. Hence the lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ are exactly the sums of shifted lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$, the polytope has the integer decomposition property, every lattice point is a Hilbert function when $n\le 3$, and lattice-point counts and Ehrhart polynomials are products of transfer matrices of the kind used in Part II. We determine the codegree of every Kozlov polytope and show that none is Gorenstein for $n\ge 3$. Finally we compare discrete and continuous invariants: the number of Hilbert functions against the volume and the lattice-point count, where we prove Kupreyeva's observed limit for the fraction of lattice points that are $f$-vectors and extend it to every rank. We also compare the centroid and second moments of the Hilbert functions with those of the polytope.

items.title: Regularity transfer for the Ritz projection
items.summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex polytope in arbitrary dimension $n\geq 1$, and consider the Ritz projection on quasi-uniform triangulations of $Ω$. We prove a new pointwise estimate in terms of the sharp maximal function and use it to establish stability in weighted Lebesgue, Orlicz, and Lorentz spaces. We then introduce discrete higher-order smoothness spaces based on oscillations and a smooth companion construction, and prove discrete analogues of classical embedding and compactness results. Finally, we establish stability of the Ritz projection in these discrete spaces, together with localized estimates. These results provide a framework for transferring higher-order regularity through the Ritz projection. As part of our analysis, we also study approximation properties of the Scott-Zhang projection in Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.

items.title: Feigin-Semikhatov duality at the critical level
