items.summary: The Feigin-Semikhatov duality asserts that the Heisenberg cosets of the subregular $W$-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ at level $k$ and the one of the principal $W$-superalgebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_{n|1}$ at level $\ell$ coincide when the levels satisfy the Feigin-Frenkel relation $(k+n)(\ell+n-1)=1$. A similar duality holds between the subregular $W$-algebra of $\mathfrak{so}_{2n+1}$ and the principal $W$-superalgebra of $\mathfrak{osp}_{2|2n}$. We study these dualities in the critical/large level limit. We describe the centerless subregular $W$-algebra at the critical level as an orbifold of the large level limit of the principal $W$-superalgebra times a lattice VOA. Our construction yields a functor between certain categories of the two involved vertex algebras. We show that in this set-up one in fact gets block-wise equivalences of categories. Studying the principal block of the large level limit of the principal $W$-superalgebra then gives us the structure of the principal blocks of the subregular $W$-algebras in the category of weight modules (which is much larger than the more common category of lower bounded modules).

items.title: Post-Hopf structures on $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and post-Lie bialgebras
items.summary: We classify post-Hopf structures on the Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, for $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not a root of unity, proving that there are exactly three isomorphism classes. We then investigate the semiclassical limits of post-Hopf quantized universal enveloping algebras and derive a compatibility condition between the induced post-Lie product and Lie cobracket. This leads to the notion of a post-Lie bialgebra. We construct a nontrivial topological post-Hopf structure on $U_\hbar(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and determine its semiclassical limit. For the standard Lie bialgebra structure on $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we classify all compatible post-Lie products up to isomorphism and show that the nontrivial class admits a quantization. Finally, we formulate the general quantization problem for post-Lie bialgebras.

items.title: Control of Complex Social Systems via Committed Minorities and Opinion Broadcast
items.summary: Complex social systems are often characterized by a deep interconnection between individuals' opinion formation and their decision-making processes. In this chapter, we show how these two dynamics can be incorporated within a unifying game-theoretic coevolutionary model for actions and opinions. We present the main theoretical results concerning the convergence of the coevolutionary model, and its recent extensions to incorporate further features of real-world social systems. Then, we focus on the problem of controlling such a coevolutionary model. In particular, we present two distinct approaches: i) introducing a committed minority in the population, and ii) broadcasting information to some target individuals. For both of these methods, we discuss their implementation and provide theoretical guarantees on their performance. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods on different case studies, illustrating their implementation on simple academic examples, as well as exploring their performance in realistic scenarios using network structures inferred from real-world data. In summary, this chapter provides an overview of the mathematical approaches developed to model a population of individuals with coevolving actions and opinions, providing effective tools to study and, ultimately, control this complex socio-technical system.

items.title: On Riemannian $r$-th order recurrent spaces
items.summary: We prove that a connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with irreducible local holonomy which is $r$-th order recurrent, $\nabla^r R=t^{(r)}\otimes R$, is locally symmetric, for every $r\ge1$. Without any assumption on the holonomy, we show that such a manifold is either locally symmetric or, locally, a flat extension $Σ^2\times\mathbb R^{n-2}$ of a surface: the only possible exceptions to local symmetry are essentially two-dimensional.

items.title: Strictly pseudoconvex $CR$ structures on $\sfS^5$ that can be turned inside out
items.summary: The existence of a complex structure on $\sfS^{6}$ implies that of strictlty pseudoconvex structures on $\sfS^{5}$ which can be turned inside out by a homotopy.

items.title: Large time decay of the fluid-structure semigroup subject to the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition
items.summary: Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. The fluid motion obeys the Navier-Stokes system, while the motion of the body is governed by the Newton law. Both motions are affected by each other at the fluid-solid interface through the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition, which is known as a substitution for the no-slip one to resolve the no-collision paradox. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. What is remarkable is that the decay structure is somewhat different under the full slip condition when the body is axially symmetric. If, in particular, the body is a ball, we then apply the linear theory developed above to the nonlinear initial value problem to show the stability of the rest state. It is, furthermore, asymptotically stable except for the full slip case.

items.title: A Polynomial Criterion for Adaptive Stabilization of Discrete-Time Stochastic Nonlinear Systems with an Unknown Input Gain
items.summary: We consider scalar discrete-time systems whose nonlinear function is a linear combination of known power functions with unknown coefficients. The input gain is nonzero and unknown, and the noise is iid zero-mean Gaussian with unknown positive variance. We show that global stabilizability is equivalent to the joint positivity of a family of polynomials determined solely by the power exponents. When this condition holds, a feedback law depending only on the exponents makes the average squared output converge almost surely to the noise variance, the smallest possible value. When the condition fails, every Borel feedback law yields divergence of the output magnitude with positive probability for some fixed parameters and a deterministic initial state.

items.title: Sharp enumeration and growth of admissible sets of integers
items.summary: A set of positive integers is admissible if equal sums of finite subsets always have equal numbers of summands. Let $a(N)$ count the nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and let $b(N)$ count those with maximum $N$. We prove $\log a(N)\sim\log b(N)\simπ\sqrt{2N/3}$, establishing the sharp logarithmic asymptotic proposed by Nicolas. More generally, let $Q_h(N)$ count the subsets for which each integer has subset-sum representations of at most $h$ distinct cardinalities. Uniformly for all positive integers $h,N$, we prove $\log Q_h(N)\asymp\min\{N,\sqrt{hN}\}$ with absolute implied constants. Every infinite set satisfying the same condition for some fixed $h$ has counting function $o(\sqrt x)$. At $h=1$, the uniform count proves the conjecture $\log a(N)\asymp\sqrt N$ of Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy, and the infinite-set theorem strengthens their conjectured vanishing lower limit to a full limit. The proofs record each subset sum together with its cardinality and use the counting theorem of Campos and the structure theorem of Carpenter, Defant and Kravitz. The sharp count also uses Nicolas's partition enumeration and an elementary construction of a long restricted-sum progression. Finally, we give an exact partition formula and asymptotics for the odd sets with separated alternate cardinality layers suggested by Nicolas, and deduce lower bounds for the number of non-stratified admissible sets.

items.title: A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
items.summary: In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

items.title: Further Generalization of Ramanujan Sums with Regular A-Functions
items.summary: In the study of Ramanujan sums, the so-called regular $A$-function is a set-valued multiplicative function that tracks certain subsets of the divisor sets of natural numbers. McCarthy provided a generalization of the Ramanujan sum using these regular $A$-function based arithmetic convolutions. This approach has recently attracted considerable interest from several researchers. In this paper, we extend McCarthy's generalization by introducing two regular $A$-functions corresponding to both parameters in the Ramanujan sum. Our generalization exhibits several properties of the Ramanujan sums. Using the regular $A$-function, We also generalize the greatest common divisor (GCD) function and the Von Sterneck formula. Our introduction of two regular $A$-functions into these expressions enables us to explore a novel perspective on the connection between these expressions and the order relation between the two regular $A$-functions. In particular, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for orthogonality and Dedekind-Hölder's identity (i.e., Ramanujan sum = Von Sterneck function) to hold. Our primary motivation for the proposed generalization is Ramanujan expansions of arithmetic functions based on arbitrary regular $A$-functions. These expansions of arbitrary $A$-functions discussed here are new in the literature.

items.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
items.summary: We prove cone restriction estimates under half-scale dimensional conditions. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we incorporate the broad restriction estimate of Ou--Wang and a localized multilinear estimate obtained through cyclic bilinear pairing and multilinear Kakeya bounds for local packet $L^2$-norm. The zero-dimensional case yields a large-value estimate on $R^{1/2}$-cubes. For certain ambient and weight dimensions, our estimates are sharp in suitable ranges of $p$, up to an $R^\varepsilon$ loss.

items.title: Preconditioning for quadratic matrix optimization via constraint reshaping
items.summary: We study quadratic optimization over orthogonality or symplectic constraints, a problem arising in eigenvalue computation, subspace analysis, and reduced-order modeling. Ill-conditioned problems have a wide positive Hessian spectrum at a minimizer, which slows first-order Riemannian methods. Existing preconditioned-metric approaches choose a Riemannian metric, which determines the resulting Hessian spectrum. We instead redesign the problem itself to find the narrowest possible spectrum. We reshape the constraints into equivalent formulations that preserve the optimal value and the solution set, giving a family of preconditioned problems parametrized by positive constraint weights. We derive a closed form for the positive Hessian spectrum in terms of these weights. Minimizing the condition number then reduces to a linear program (LP) in the logarithms of the weights. The LP attains a globally optimal design within the paired equal-block family, and its strong duality gives matching lower bounds on the condition number. On tested instances, the optimized formulation substantially reduces the local condition number, with returned spectra matching predictions on both orthogonal and symplectic instances. We also benchmark the design against Lagrangian and left-right preconditioned metrics. The method thus provides an exact, optimization-based alternative to heuristic preconditioned metrics.

items.title: Between proper and strong edge-colorings of graphs with maximum degree at most four
items.summary: A $(1^j,2^k)$-packing edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of its edge set $E(G)$ into $j$ matchings and $k$ induced matchings. It can be viewed as intermediate colorings between proper and strong edge-coloring. The study of this topic on subcubic graphs has drawn considerable attention recently, with many conjectures and open problems proposed and resolved. However, very few results are known for graphs with maximum degree four or more. Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana showed that every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{19})$-packing edge-coloring and a $(1^2,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. In this paper, we improve the results of Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana by showing every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. As a corollary of our result, every graph with degree at most four has a $(1^2,2^{16})$-packing edge-coloring.

items.title: Mahler measures and a cubic Dedekind zeta value in three dilogarithms
items.summary: A general formula evaluates a three-variable Mahler measure at Heegner points of fundamental discriminant $-d$, with $d>3$ and $d\equiv3\pmod8$, using CM modular forms and ray class $L$-values. Together with the case $d=27$, it proves six identities conjectured by Zheng. The parameter at $d=163$ also occurs in a cubic Ramanujan-Sato series for $1/π$. For $C=\mathbb Q(a)$, where $a^3+2a-2=0$, an exact hyperbolic volume argument expresses the Dedekind zeta derivative $ζ_C'(-1)$ in three Bloch-Wigner dilogarithms. The analogous identity for $C(\sqrt5)$ remains conjectural and is reduced to one explicit Bloch-group equality.

items.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
items.summary: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.

items.title: Twisted Verlinde formulas for cyclic orbifolds and the order-two simple current of a vertex operator superalgebra
items.summary: Let $V=\Vev\oplus J$ be a simple vertex operator superalgebra with $\Vev$ simple, rational and $C_2$-cofinite, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic group acting faithfully on $\Vev$. For arbitrary twisted $V$-modules we prove: (1) for $G$ of arbitrary order, a twisted Verlinde formula for $\Vev$; (2) unitarity of the orbifold $S$-matrix block in generating sectors; (3) as a consequence, a formula for $N^{X_3}_{X_1,X_2}\pm N^{J\boxtimes X_3}_{X_1,X_2}$ as sums over $J$-orbits of $G$-stable untwisted modules, in which $J$-fixed points enter with weight two and in the minus sign, with a parity selection rule (read in $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$) and a dimension sum rule; (4) simplicity of $V^G$. These results concern the $G$-graded fusion category of $\Vev$ together with the order two invertible object $J$ with $θ_J=-\dim_qJ$. The statements are tested numerically on six examples (odd and even orders up to $15$, both signs of $\dim_qJ$, $J$-fixed modules).

items.title: Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
items.summary: We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_β$ to $A^p_α$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_β$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_β$. Moreover, $A^q_β \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_β$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_α]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_γ] \subset [T_{g},A^p_α]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

items.title: Convergence of adaptive boundary element methods driven by functional a posteriori error estimates
items.summary: The recent work [Kurz et al., Numer. Math., 147 (2021)] proposed functional a posteriori error estimates for boundary element methods (BEMs) together with a related adaptive mesh-refinement strategy. Unlike most a posteriori BEM error estimators, the proposed functional error estimators cover Galerkin as well as collocation BEM and, more importantly, do not control the error in the integral density on the boundary, but the error of the potential approximation in the domain, which is of greater relevance in practice. The estimates rely on the numerical solution of auxiliary problems on auxiliary strip domains along the boundary, where the strips are affected by the adaptive mesh-refinement and hence vary. For Galerkin BEM, we prove that the proposed adaptive mesh-refinement algorithm yields convergence of the potential error to zero. Due to the structural difference to residual-based estimators, the proof requires new ideas.

items.title: Exponential generating functions of multiple polylogarithms at arbitrary integer indices
items.summary: We give an explicit formula expressing any finite product of depth-one polylogarithms at arbitrary integer indices as a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of shuffle-type multivariable multiple polylogarithms. The proof starts with an exponential generating function. For any fixed positive multi-index $\mathbf{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$, the substitution $z_i\mapsto z_i\exp(x_1+\cdots+x_i)$ in the corresponding shuffle-type multiple polylogarithm yields the exponential generating function for the functions at indices $\mathbf{s}-\mathbf{k}$, where $\mathbf{k}$ ranges over $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^r$. We combine this identity with the shuffle product for iterated integrals at positive indices and compare coefficients to obtain the product formula. The appendix gives an alternative proof using the Euler differential operators $z_i\partial/\partial z_i$.

items.title: Double determinants of quaternion matrices in the P-generalized determinant framework with applications
items.summary: Building on the P-generalized determinant over quaternions, we introduce the double determinant of arbitrary square quaternion matrices. We then apply the double determinant to obtain a determinant representation for the inverse of any invertible quaternion matrix, without the Hermitian restriction. Furthermore, we establish Cramer's rule for the unique solutions to the quaternion linear equations Ax=b and xA=b, as well as to the quaternion matrix equations AX=B, XA=B, and AXB=C. As an application, we use the determinant representation of the unique solution to AXB=C to design a color image encryption-decryption scheme. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the encryption algorithm effectively conceals the contour and color information of the original image, while the decryption algorithm restores the original image almost perfectly, thereby confirming the effectiveness and practical potential of the proposed scheme.

items.title: The Cesàro Value Iteration
items.summary: In this paper, we consider undiscouted infinite-horizon optimal control for deterministic systems with an uncountable state and input space. We specifically address the case when the classic value iteration does not converge. For such systems, we use the Ces`aro mean to define the infinite-horizon optimal control problem and the corresponding infinite-horizon value function. Moreover, for this value function, we introduce the Cesàro value iteration and prove its convergence for the special case of systems with periodic optimal operating behavior. For this instance, we also show that the Cesàro value function recovers the undiscounted infinite-horizon optimal cost, if the latter is well-defined.

items.title: A variational theory for von Kármán vortex streets
items.summary: We construct von Kármán vortex streets as global kinetic energy maximizers for the 2D Euler flow in an infinite periodic channel: our variational framework imposes no a prior symmetry, support constraints, or sign conditions on the admissible class. More specifically, under $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ constraint of the absolute vorticity maximum with other natural constraints, we show that the maximizers are traveling pairs of simply connected vortex patches of support radius $O(\varepsilon)$, converging to the von Kármán point-vortex configuration satisfying glide reflection symmetry as $\varepsilon \to 0$. We prove nonlinear stability of the von Kármán streets under a bound on the vertical support, using a compactness result valid for more general assumptions. Furthermore, we construct slightly tilted asymmetric von Kármán vortex streets as energy maximizers under a tilted moment constraint.

items.title: A polyptych of multi-centered deformation spaces
items.summary: Extending Verdier's deformation space to the normal cone of a closed subscheme and Rost's double deformation space of a pair of nested closed subschemes, we introduce a notion of deformation spaces attached to chains of immersions of arbitrary lengths $n$. One main result, which builds on the formalism of multi-centered dilatations of schemes, is the existence of so-called panelization isomorphisms, which produce under suitable regularity conditions several canonical isomorphisms between a given deformation space of length $n$ and some deformation spaces of smaller lengths. Having these panelization isomorphisms also allows to give geometric descriptions of the strata -- certain restrictions of special interest -- of deformation spaces.

items.title: Minkowskian open/closed conformal field theory possibly without vacuum: the Cardy case
items.summary: For any conformal net, not necessarily rational, we construct the associated Cardy-type conformal field theory on the Minkowski spacetimes $(\mathbb R/2π\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb R$ for closed strings and $[0,π]\times\mathbb R$ for open strings within the framework of algebraic quantum field theory. In addition to verifying some of their basic properties, we prove three forms of Haag duality for multi-double-cones and boundary intervals, interpreted respectively as the Minkowskian versions of modular invariance, the Cardy consistency condition, and the Morita equivalence of boundary field algebras.

items.title: Sharp minimax rates and adaptive estimation of latent proportions in bivariate Poisson mixtures
items.summary: We study estimation of the mean latent composition in a bivariate Poisson mixture. Conditional on an unobserved intensity S and proportion U, two counts are independent Poisson variables with respective means SU and S(1-U). The mixing law is unrestricted on the Cartesian product [a,b] x [0,1], where a and b are finite constants satisfying 0 < a < b, and dependence between S and U is allowed. Although the mixing distribution is identifiable, the usual ratio of mean counts estimates an intensity-weighted proportion and may be biased for theta = E[U]. We construct polynomial estimators based on factorial moments and establish the exact leading exponent of the minimax squared-error risk on the logarithmic scale, without claiming an exact multiplicative minimax constant. We also derive the sharp logarithmic separation exponent for testing zero latent covariance and construct an adaptive estimator achieving parametric squared-error risk on the zero-covariance submodel while retaining the optimal full-model logarithmic minimax exponent. Simulations illustrate the bias-variance trade-off, the role of polynomial regularization, and the distinction between theoretically guaranteed and empirically calibrated adaptation.

items.title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
items.summary: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $π_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

items.title: Shape theory for condensed anima
items.summary: We give different perspectives on the notion of shape for condensed anima. We prove that it recovers more classical notions of shape not only for all locally compact Hausdorff but also locally contractible spaces. These recovering statements imply and extend comparison results on sheaf and condensed cohomology by Clausen-Scholze and Haine. Another homotopy-theoretical direction for condensed anima are their condensed homotopy groups. Connected to this, we give a description of the underlying topological group functor on condensed groups via quasi-topological groups.

items.title: Optimal Beurling-Hörmander-type uncertainty principles and nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces
items.summary: We study how rapidly a nonzero function $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and its Fourier transform $\widehat{f}$ can simultaneously decay. For each suitable weight function $ω$, we construct a convex weight function $\varpi$ and establish the existence of a threshold $Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)} \in (0, \infty)$, where $\varpi^*$ denotes the convex conjugate of $\varpi$. For $a,b > 0$, the conditions \[ \int_{-\infty}^\infty |f(x)| e^{ω(a|x|)} \, \mathrm{d}x < \infty \qquad \text{and} \qquad \int_{-\infty}^\infty |\widehat{f}(ξ)| e^{\varpi^*(b|ξ|)} \, \mathrm{d}ξ < \infty \] force $f = 0$ when $ab > Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$, whereas the functions satisfying both conditions form a dense subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ when $ab < Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$. Similar results are also established in higher dimensions. We characterize the weights $ω$ for which $\varpi$ is equivalent to $ω$ and use this to determine when the Beurling-Hörmander uncertainty principle is optimal. A discrete form of the same construction yields a characterization of the nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces $\mathcal{S}^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $Σ^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ in terms of their defining weight sequences $M$ and $A$, under suitable regularity assumptions.

items.title: Benders Cut Filtering for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Robustness Scenarios and Topology Switching
items.summary: Many large-scale optimization problems decompose into a master problem and scenario subproblems. Benders decomposition exploits this structure by iteratively solving the subproblems and adding constraints, called Benders cuts, to the master problem. We study Benders cut filtering: given a set of Benders cuts produced in one iteration, which subset should be added to the master problem? Adding all generated cuts can cause rapid master problem growth, whereas retaining fewer cuts may require more Benders iterations. To our knowledge, few prior works have studied this question for Benders cuts. Classical cut filtering techniques require modification because Benders cuts enforce constraints omitted from the master problem, whereas conventional cutting planes are optional inequalities that strengthen the relaxation. We propose violation-based filtering, diversity-based filtering via k-medoids clustering on cosine distances, and a hybrid that selects a most-violated cut per cluster. We compare these strategies with no filtering, random filtering, and our adaptation of SCIP's hybrid cut selector on an affine potential-based flow problem with topology switching and robustness scenarios. On instances solved by all configurations, our hybrid approach reduces the shifted geometric mean solve time by about 45% compared to no filtering, and by 39% compared to our adaptation of SCIP's hybrid cut selector. While violation-based filtering achieves a similar runtime, the hybrid approach requires about 17% fewer callback rounds. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Benders cut filtering on this problem class and motivate evaluation in other domains.

items.title: An improved Moore bound for girths seven and eleven
items.summary: Let $n(d,k)$ be the minimum number of vertices of a graph of minimum degree $d$ and girth at least $g=2k+1$. A simple counting argument gives the classical lower bound $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)=1+d\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(d-1)^i$, known as the Moore bound and dating back at least to 1960. Apart from complete graphs and odd cycles, graphs attaining this lower bound can exist only for girth $5$ and degrees $3,7$ and $57$ (Hoffman and Singleton 1960; Bannai and Ito 1973; Damerell 1973). Nevertheless, for more than sixty years this lower bound has not been substantially improved beyond an additive constant. For $k\geq 3$, i.e. girth at least $7$, the best general bound was $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)+2$, due to Bannai and Ito (1981). We show that for fixed girth $7$ and growing degree $d$ we have $n(d,3)\ge m(d,3)+(1-o(1))d/8$. Furthermore, for girth $11$ we have $n(d,5)\ge m(d,5)+Ω(d^{3/5})$. In particular, the excess $n(d,k)-m(d,k)$, for $k\in\{3,5\}$, tends to infinity with $d$ and is therefore generally unbounded, which answers a question of Bollobás from 1978. For the degree/diameter problem we obtain similar bounds. A graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $3$ or $5$ has at most $m(d,3)-Ω(\sqrt{d})$ or $m(d,5)-Ω(d^{3/10})$ vertices, respectively. This answers a question of Bermond and Bollobás from 1981: for every constant $c$ there are $d$ and $k$ such that every graph of maximum degree $d$ and diameter $k$ has at least $c$ fewer vertices than the Moore bound.

items.title: Stars and paths in oriented graphs
items.summary: Let $\overrightarrow{F}$ be a fixed oriented graph. Its oriented Turán number, written $\exo(n,\overrightarrow{F})$, is the largest size of an $n$-vertex oriented graph with no copy of $\overrightarrow{F}$. This parameter extends the classical notion of Turán number to oriented graphs. In this paper, we investigate the supersaturation results for the directed path $P_k~(k\geq 2)$ and all oriented stars $\overrightarrow{S}_{p,q}~(0\leq p\leq q$), and all oriented paths of order at most four.

items.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
items.summary: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid, the elongated triangular grid and the snub hexagonal grid. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid. As a by-product, we prove that every identifying code of a cubic graph with the slow growth property in which every vertex lies on exactly one triangle (resp. $4$-cycle) has density at least $2/3$ (resp. $3/7$).

items.title: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere
items.summary: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which the positive residue characteristics of $S$ are invertible. We identify Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients with the category of modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The equivalence takes the free module on a smooth $S$-scheme to its motive with transfers and commutes with pullback and extension of coefficients. It applies to singular and nonreduced schemes and to mixed-characteristic bases. The main geometric input is the base change stability of Voevodsky's motivic Eilenberg--MacLane spectrum $HR_S$. We prove this using permutation quotients of tori, families of relative cycles and arithmetic power homotopies. The identification over fields and the reconstruction theorem of Cisinski--Déglise then give the module equivalence.

items.title: On the dimension of $V$-variable fractals
items.summary: Random recursive sets have been used to model a wide range of fractal phenomena, but they can be slow and difficult to generate. $V$-variability address this problem by allowing these sets at most $V$ distinct shapes at each level of magnification. The formulae for the almost sure Hausdorff dimension of both classes is known, and it has been conjectured that (under mild assumptions) the $V$-variable dimension converges to the random recursive dimension as $V\to\infty$. We prove this conjecture.

items.title: On the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with toroidal cylinders and their apparent contours
items.summary: We study the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with toroidal cylinders $S^1(r) \times \mathbb{R}^2$. We relate the contact type to the singularities of the corresponding parallel projections along the direction of the axes of the toroidal cylinders, the geometry of the apparent contours under these projections, and the geometry of the original surfaces.

items.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
items.summary: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. A novelty of our method is building a connection between the $s$-principal submatrix problem and low-rank singular value perturbations. We also provide an algorithm to determine a positive definite matrix that realizes the given global and local symplectic spectra. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

items.title: Conditional propagation of chaos for systems of particles with polynomial interactions
items.summary: We consider N interacting particles taking values in the real numbers and evolving in discrete time with time step 1/n. Each particle follows an individual dynamics, driven by its own noise, which depends on the total configuration via a polynomial interaction. Moreover, all particles receive the same collective perturbation. This perturbation is given by a multilinear homogeneous sum of order $ m \geq 2$ of independent centered random fields which are evaluated at the current positions of the particles. We show that, as N and n tend to infinity, the system converges to the solution of a conditional McKean-Vlasov equation which is driven by an additional Brownian motion which emerges in the limit from the collective perturbations. Moreover we give explicit bounds for the Wasserstein-2-distance. Our proof combines the invariance principle of Mossel, O'Donnell and Oleszkiewicz (2010), the CLT for Wiener chaoses in the Wasserstein-2-form of Ledoux, Nourdin and Peccati (2015) and a conditional law of large numbers for weighted U-statistics proven in this paper.

items.title: The construction of a regular non-Berwald Landsberg surface
items.summary: We construct a regular non-Berwald Landsberg metric of zero flag curvature on an open subset of the plane via a periodically forced oscillator equation. We solve the associated return equation exactly to obtain closed, strongly convex coindicatrices. Starting from a finite truncation of a formal control, we use a uniform local inverse for a periodic comparison operator and a smoothing iteration to make the return map of the original oscillator equal to the identity on the chosen base neighborhood. A direct calculation of the spray exhibits a nonzero component of the Berwald tensor.

items.title: Embedding lattices of quasivarieties of periodic groups into lattices of additively idempotent semiring varieties: An algebraic proof
items.summary: A general result by Jackson (Flat algebras and the translation of universal Horn logic to equational logic, J. Symb. Log. 73(1) (2008) 90--128) implies that the lattice of all quasivarieties of groups of exponent dividing $n$ embeds into the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$ of all varieties of additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups are unions of groups of exponent dividing $n$; the image of this embedding is an interval in $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$. We provide a new, direct, and purely algebraic proof of these facts and present a new identity basis for the top variety of the interval. In addition, we obtain new information about the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$, demonstrating that the properties of the lattice for $n\ge 3$ differ drastically from those previously known when $n=1$ or $2$.

items.title: High-Order Area-Preserving Runge--Kutta Methods for Surface Diffusion Flow of Curves
items.summary: We propose a class of high-order area-preserving Runge--Kutta (RK) methods for the surface diffusion flow of curves, a curvature-driven geometric flow that decreases the perimeter while conserving the enclosed area. By coupling the parametric finite element approximation of the classical BGN formulation with symplectic RK time discretisation, we rigorously prove that the fully discrete scheme unconditionally conserves the enclosed area of curves. This conservation arises solely from the intrinsic symplectic structure of the RK methods, without introducing any additional constraints, auxiliary variables, or Lagrange multipliers to enforce structure preservation. To attain high temporal accuracy, we adopt $q$-stage Gauss RK methods, which are symplectic and yield order $2q$ (e.g., $q=1,2,3$). The resulting fully implicit, strongly nonlinear system is solved efficiently via an equivalent discrete formulation combined with a monolithic damped Newton iteration. Extensive numerical tests on various evolving curves validate the theoretical findings, confirming exact area preservation, high-order temporal convergence, and favorable mesh quality, while the Newton iteration count rapidly decreases to fewer than 8 per step, demonstrating the robustness of the tailored solver.

items.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
items.summary: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $Λ_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partialΛ_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question has recently been settled, $Λ_4=S_4$, by computer-assisted proofs of D. Z. Liu and L. Marshall; Liu also proved that $Λ_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $Λ_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

items.title: Critical nonlocal GJMS operator on odd dimensional spheres and mean field equation
items.summary: For a smooth axially symmetric function on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with $n\geq 1$, in odd dimensions we prove a neat formula for the critical nonlocal GJMS operator $P_n$ similar to the one in even dimensions. With this formula, we give a simple proof of the Liouville theorem by Gui-Hu-Xie (J. Funct. Anal. 2022): Every smooth axially symmetric solution to $$\frac{1}{n+1} P_n u = (n-1)!(e^{nu}-1) \quad \mathrm{on} \quad \mathbb{S}^n,n\geq 2$$ is identically zero, without using any delicate property of Gegenbauer polynomials.

items.title: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
items.summary: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo. For a related family of lattice-polarized $K3$ surfaces, we give a geometric realization of the ring of meromorphic modular forms with prescribed poles and trivial character and describe the corresponding Looijenga compactification.

items.title: A family of homogeneous convex non-scattering domains with analytic non-circular boundaries
items.summary: A homogeneous planar non-scattering domain is a bounded medium with a constant material coefficient that produces no scattered field for some nonzero entire solution of the Helmholtz equation at a particular wave number. It is known that the boundary of such a domain must be real analytic at all points where the incident field does not vanish. Previously, disks were the only known examples. We construct a family of homogeneous strictly convex non-scattering domains that are neither disks nor ellipses. The family bifurcates from a particular non-scattering disk, with the boundary, wave number, and constant coefficient varying along the branch. The construction uses a conformal change of variables and analytic bifurcation theory applied to the resulting nonlinear problem.

items.title: Minimal primes and radicality of join-meet ideals of modular lattices with one diamond
items.summary: Let $L$ be a finite modular lattice with exactly one diamond, that is, exactly one interval of length two with at least three atoms. We describe the minimal primes of the join-meet ideal $I_L$ in terms of maximal closed distributive sublattices of $L$, and we show that $I_L$ has height $|L|-\mathrm{rank}(L)$. Moreover, we characterize the radicality of $I_L$, over any field, in terms of the complements of the atoms of the diamond in their fibres. Finally, we prove that $I_L$ is unmixed if and only if all its minimal primes have the same height, if and only if the rank of every maximal closed distributive sublattice through an atom of the diamond is $\mathrm{rank}(L)-1$; in this case $I_L$ is radical.

items.title: Rational maps with at most three critical values have no Herman rings
items.summary: We prove that any rational map with at most three critical values has no Herman rings. This generalizes previous results of Shishikura and Milnor on bi-critical rational maps.

items.title: A Game-Theoretic Characterization of Feedback Capability for Fully Coupled Vector-Valued Nonparametric Systems
items.summary: We study feedback stabilization for the discrete-time system $x_{t+1}=f(x_t)+u_t+w_{t+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unknown $f$ and arbitrary bounded disturbances. For scalar plants, the sharp feedback capability threshold under generalized Lipschitz uncertainty is $\frac{3}{2}+\sqrt{2}$. We treat fully coupled vector-valued systems, where scalar order and interval recursion are unavailable and coupling precludes a coordinatewise reduction. We introduce a response-history escape game whose adversarial objective requires a finite envelope and an unbounded state radius. Borel determinacy, invariance under a change of finite initial history, and slope monotonicity define a game value $Γ_d$. One causal feedback law stabilizes every plant in the uncertainty class against every bounded disturbance sequence whenever $L<Γ_d$. At every $L\geΓ_d$, each causal feedback law and each initial state admit a globally $Γ_d$-Lipschitz plant whose state norms tend to infinity with zero disturbances. Thus stabilization is possible exactly below the critical value. We also prove $Γ_d=1+(\log d)/(2d)+O((\log\log d)/d)$, with explicit coefficients in bounds on both sides of the remainder. Explicit finite-dimensional bounds give $Γ_d>1$ in every dimension and $Γ_2\ge 7/5$. A nearest-neighbor law achieves the planar guarantee. The values are nonincreasing in dimension, and comparison with the scalar theory yields $Γ_1=\frac{3}{2}+\sqrt{2}$.

items.title: The Csisz{á}r order for ranking the importance of input random variables
items.summary: Csisz{á}r indices $S\_f(X,Y)$, defined as the $f$-divergence between the joint distribution of a general random couple $(X,Y)$ and the product of its marginal distributions, are widely used to quantify dependence between the input variable $X$ and the output variable $Y$. We show that the ranking of two input variables $X$ and $X'$ in terms of their importance w.r.t.\ the output variable, given by the comparison of the Csisz{á}r indices $S\_f(X,Y)$ and $S\_f(X',Y)$ depends on the choice of $f$. We introduce the Csisz{á}r order of input variables as the uniform ordering of Csisz{á}r indices over all proper convex functions $f$. We give a sufficient condition to prove Csiszár order of two input multivariate random variables. We fully characterize it in two cases: when $(X,X',Y)$ is a Gaussian vector (in the one-dimensional case this amount to compare the square of their correlation); and when $X$, $X'$ and $Y$ are Bernoulli random variables. Finally, motivated by sensitivity analysis, we show that, when $(X,X',Y)$ is a three-dimensional Gaussian random vector, thresholding $X$, $X'$, and $Y$ either preserves the Csisz{á}r order or makes the input variables incomparable; in particular thresholding never reverses the ranking.

items.title: Two Knuth orbits of order 256 without primitive semifield coordinatizations
items.summary: We exhibit two Knuth orbits of semifield planes of order 256 in which every coordinatizing semifield is nonprimitive on both the left and the right. Each orbit consists of two isotopy classes. The first orbit contains 168 isomorphism classes of unital semifields and the second contains 32. We give binary multiplication matrices for a representative of each orbit and an exhaustive computation that verifies nonprimitivity and the counts directly from these matrices.

items.title: $p$-adic Fourier theory for unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and weighted Monna maps
items.summary: We generalize a recent result of Ardakov and Berger on the $p$-adic valuations of Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials evaluated at Lubin--Tate periods over the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For finite unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of degree $f \geq 2$, we introduce a weighted analogue of the Monna map and show that it determines the valuations of these polynomial values for Lubin--Tate formal groups whose formal logarithms are $p$-typical. Our proof uses the Artin--Hasse exponential and Witt vectors. As an application, for a distinguished Lubin--Tate formal group, we determine the exact norms of the associated Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials on Banach spaces of locally analytic functions and obtain an explicit rescaling of the Banach basis constructed by Bannai and Kobayashi so that each basis element has norm one.

items.title: On the Maximum Number of Vertices that Belong to Every Metric Basis
items.summary: Resolving sets of graphs have been widely studied since their introduction in the 1970's by Slater and, independently, by Harary and Melter. The minimum cardinality of a resolving set of a graph $G$ is called the metric dimension of $G$ and is denoted by $\dim(G)$. In this paper, we concentrate on the existence of vertices in a graph $G$ that belong to all metric bases of $G$, i.e. resolving sets of cardinality $\dim(G)$. Such vertices are called basis forced vertices, and we denote the number of them by $\mathrm{bf}(G)$. We show that $\mathrm{bf}(G)\le 2/3(n-\dim(G)-1)$ for any connected nontrivial graph $G$ of order $n$. In addition, we show that this bound can be attained. Furthermore, it also implies that $\mathrm{bf}(G)\le 2/5(n-1)$ holds for any nontrivial connected graph $G$. This result answers a question posed by Bagheri \emph{et al.} in 2016. Moreover, we provide a complete realization of the parameters $n$, $\dim(G)$ and $\mathrm{bf}(G) \ge 1$ within the previous bounds. We consider some extremal cases related to basis forced vertices in a graph, in particular, we give a full characterization of the graphs with $\mathrm{bf}(G) = 2$ and $\dim(G) = n-4$.

items.title: Uniform Bounds of $F$-Signature and Effective Ideal Containments
items.summary: We establish inequalities between numerical invariants and ideal containments in local rings containing a field. We prove the positivity of $F$-signature for klt-type algebras essentially of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ under prime characteristic reduction and resolve the Uniform Symbolic Topology Problem effectively for both $F$-finite strongly $F$-regular rings of prime characteristic and klt type algebras over $\mathbb{C}$. Consequently, letting $s(R)$ denote the $F$-signature and $d$ the Krull dimension, if $d\geq 2$ then $I^{\left(\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq \overline{I^{n}}$ and $I^{\left(d\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq I^n$ for every ideal $I \subseteq R$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$ in these settings.

items.title: Removable forests in $k$-connected and $k$-edge-connected graphs
items.summary: We prove the forest conjecture of Clay and Jordán: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $F$ be a forest with $m$ vertices and $e$ edges. If a $k$-connected graph $G$ has minimum degree at least $\max\{k+e,m-1\}$, then it contains a copy of $F$ whose edge deletion preserves $k$-connectivity. We also prove the $k$-edge-connectivity version.

items.title: Proof of Stanley's Conjecture on the Leading Ehrhart Coefficients of the Birkhoff Polytope
items.summary: Let $c(n,k)$ denote the coefficient of $r^{(n-1)^2-k}$ in the Ehrhart polynomial of the $n\times n$ Birkhoff polytope. For every fixed nonnegative integer $k$, we prove that $c(n,k)/c(n,0)\sim n^{3k}/(2^k k!)$ as $n\to\infty$, confirming a conjecture of Stanley.

items.title: A note on a nonlocal antisymmetric barrier
items.summary: In this note, we present a barrier function for an equation involving the fractional Laplacian in the antisymmetric setting, providing an explicit inequality in the full positivity set of the function. This leads to an improvement of the quantitative maximum principle given in [DPTV26], where the bound was obtained in a strict subset of its positivity set and required additional assumptions on lower order coefficients. As a consequence of this, we give an optimal lower bound on the growth of antisymmetric solutions from the symmetry hyperplane.

items.title: PWLNet: A Framework for Linearized Neural Surrogates in Nonlinear Process Optimization
items.summary: Neural networks represent nonlinear process systems accurately, but embedding them in optimization is difficult because smooth activations introduce nonlinear, nonconvex constraints. PWLNet is a Python framework for building optimization-compatible neural surrogates through exact and piecewise-linear reformulations. It combines baseline and physics-informed training, optimization-aware pruning, and Pyomo embeddings based on ReLU mixed-integer linear models, exact tanh nonlinear models, PWL-tanh formulations, and binary-free SOSX branch-and-LP. PWL-native training uses the same activation in training and embedding, avoiding extra linearization error. It is evaluated on Boston housing, the Williams-Otto process, the Van de Vusse reactor, and a hydroformylation semi-batch reactor. On Boston housing, SOSX training gave the best common-architecture model (test MAE 1.984, R2 = 0.925). On Williams-Otto, pruning 15% of hidden neurons reduced MILP solution time 6.5-fold while preserving the selected operating point. For the Van de Vusse reactor, a physics-informed ReLU RNN pruned from 32 to 12 hidden units enabled tractable exact MILP embedding and a 4% true-plant economic gain over the best ramp-and-hold policy, while terminal-aware shrinking-horizon prediction reached 99.7% of the direct-shooting reference. For the hydroformylation reactor, one-step exact-tanh IPOPT reached 99.2% of the certified reference product with peak pressure 20.002 bar (limit 20 bar) and 14.36 s total solve time over 280 moves; ReLU and PWL-native controllers achieved comparable recovery, with ReLU fastest. Longer horizons and physics-informed training did not consistently improve closed-loop results. Overall, compact linearized neural surrogates enable accurate, tractable optimization in steady-state and dynamic applications, with constraint fidelity identified as a key direction for improvement.

items.title: Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics
items.summary: We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(μ)$, where the Gibbs measure $μ$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(μ)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincaré inequality in the velocity variable.

items.title: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
items.summary: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

items.title: Survival of the fittest Cox model: Pivotal variable selection for time-to-event data
items.summary: We revisit Cox's proportional hazards model to improve variable selection in survival analysis. A square-root transformation of the partial likelihood renders the selection of the regularization parameter asymptotically pivotal: the baseline hazard and the censoring rate cancel exactly, and the way censoring is spread over time only enters through a bounded correction of order $1/\log n$. Using martingale residuals, we compute this penalty level by Monte Carlo without reordering the design matrix. The resulting criterion borrows from information criteria such as BIC and from penalized regression methods such as the lasso, taking the best of both. On simulated and real data, our method substantially improves upon state-of-the-art approaches used daily.

items.title: Schubert Calculus in the Eye of the Storm
items.summary: We introduce new combinatorial objects, called storm diagrams, to study the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of complete flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/B$. We consider the quantum product of an arbitrary Schubert class with a modified Hirzebruch $λ_y$-class of a tautological subbundle. We show that its Schubert expansion coefficients are given by the total weights of storm diagrams. As applications, we establish Pieri rules for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of partial flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/P$. Our storm diagrams provide the first combinatorial model for a manifestly positive multiplication formula for partial flag varieties beyond the Chevalley case, with restrictions imposed on only one of the two Schubert classes.

items.title: Parafermi algebra and semiprimality
items.summary: The principles of rational parafermi algebra of Mersenne order $p=2^n-1$, developed in an earlier work, are recapitulated in the introduction: A Continued Kronecker Square-root process (CKS) dispenses with irrational numbers.The process creates two types of lower triangular square matrices, called of $G$-type and $J$-type, whose elements decompose Catalan numbers in particular ways. Trilinear relations, which have the lower-left matrix part interact with a suitably chosen block-diagonal part, are only semi-conservative in that $G$-type and $J$-type elements are preserved but appear in an operational context showing different direction of rotation. The second section begins with an examination of the immersion effect, a tendency of LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(p')})$ (for $G$-like lower-left part at order $p'\hspace*{-0.8mm}:=2^{n+1}\hspace*{-0.5mm}-\hspace*{-0.5mm}1$) to adopt pecularities of LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$: a semiprime in LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(15)})$ leads to a semiprime in LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(31)})$; diagonally repeated semiprimes in LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(31)})$ prompt diagonally repeated semiprimes in LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(63)})$. After translating opposing directions of rotation to differently directed paths that emerge when the ordinal number of the second factor of a semiprime with first factor 3, 7 or 11 is varied, a rulebook is formulated which reveals that paths associated with LL$(J_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$ are not only aimed differently; they occur five times as often as paths associated with LL$(G_{μ,ν}^{(p)})$. The coincidence of the frequency ratio ${\cal G}^{(p)}/{\cal J}^{(p)}$ with the mass ratio of conventional matter over dark matter is commented upon at the close.

items.title: A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions
items.summary: We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{u<a\}$ and $\{u>b\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares. Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$. The minimum number $m_3(N)$ of nonzero values in $Q_N$ among whole-lattice harmonic functions nonzero at the origin satisfies $m_3(N)=(1+o(1))(2N+1)^2$. More generally, if a fixed nonzero harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ has $O(N^2)$ nonzero values in $Q_N$ along a sequence $N\to\infty$, then its support has a unique irredundant cover by finitely many characteristic planes. If there are $k$ such planes, the support count in $Q_N$ is $k(2N+1)^2+O_u(N)$.

items.title: Anytime-valid goodness-of-fit test by $e$-spacings
items.summary: To perform an anytime-valid goodness-of-fit test, we propose spacing-based \(e\)-processes that control the type-I error rate under arbitrary stopping rules. Based on the maximum spacing of order statistics, we construct spacing-based \(e\)-processes for nonparametrically testing distribution. The resulting procedures are simple and computationally efficient, and are power-consistent. We call them $e$-spacing tests. This approach is especially powerful in detecting localized discrepancy between the data-generating density and the null density. Under mild conditions, the logarithm of the proposed \(e\)-process is asymptotically equivalent to that of the oracle-optimal \(e\)-process. We further generalize the construction from maximal spacing to maximum spacing set in the form of the \(1/k\) fraction of the largest \(m\)th order spacings, as a measure of the lower-level set of density. It boosts power under more global discrepancy from the null. Furthermore, we propose a greedy predictable scheme, via argmax or softmax rules, to combine multiple $e$-spacing testing strategies. We prove that it optimally tunes the $e$-spacing test. The proposed approach is readily generalizable to multivariate testing via a coordinate-wise Rosenblatt-transform. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed methods perform favorably relative to the considered anytime-valid competitors as well as various types of multiple test-adjusted Kolmogorov--Smirnov tests.

items.title: Settling the no-$(k+1)$-in-line problem when $k$ is not small
items.summary: What is the maximum number of points that can be selected from an $n\times n$ square lattice so that no $k+1$ of them are collinear? This was asked more than $100$ years ago for $k=2$ and it remained wide open ever since. In this paper, we prove the exact answer is $kn$, provided that $ n\ge k\ge C\log n$ for an absolute constant $C<20$. The proof relies on carefully constructed block-uniform random bipartite graphs and concentration inequalities.

items.title: Notes on modules of finite injective dimension
items.summary: Motivated by Bass' conjecture, we study finitely generated modules of finite injective dimension and the additional constraints they impose on the ambient ring. Beyond ensuring the Cohen--Macaulay property, the presence of such modules enforces further conditions on the ring, including reducedness, normality, being an integral domain, and various singularity conditions such as complete intersection, Gorenstein, and beyond. This continues to detect non-singularity as well. We also address the reflexivity (and also torsionlessness) of modules with finite injective dimension and show that this forces the ring to be quasi-normal. In the same vein, we investigate the injective dimension of tensor products and endomorphism rings. Finally, we study the behavior of R when high syzygies of ksurject onto a non-zero R-module of finite injective dimension.

items.title: Agnostic Smoothed Online Regression with Adversarial Responses
items.summary: We study smoothed online prediction with bounded adversarial responses. This widely studied framework bridges i.i.d. sampling and adversarial covariate selection through a smoothness parameter $\textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}}$, which bounds conditional covariate densities relative to a fixed, unknown base measure. We propose Hedge-Cover, an information-theoretic algorithm that achieves sublinear regret $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\text{Pdim}(\mathcal{F}) \textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}} T})$ for function classes with bounded pseudo-dimension. The algorithm aggregates a carefully constructed family of experts using Hedge, with a prior that links regret to the number of disagreements between a consistent selector and a target function. We bound this number by exploiting covariate smoothness. This answers an open problem posed in \cite{blanchard2025agnostic} on the minimax optimal adaptive regret of the smoothed online regression problem. We establish a matching lower bound for the class of linear predictors. The main intricacy of the lower bound lies in explicitly constructing a challenging sequential covariate distribution supported on mutually orthogonal hyperplanes. This construction may be of independent technical interest. Finally, we revisit the well-specified setting and quantify the effect of response noise. For conditionally $ν^2$-subGaussian responses, we extend the existing lower bound under realizable responses by showing that the minimax expected regret is $Ω((1\vee ν)\sqrt{(\textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}}-1)dT})$ for a function class of VC dimension $d$. A corresponding upper bound for ERM matches this dependence on $ν$.

items.title: On the solution of a question for meromorphic functions sharing three values IM and a fourth value CM in the complex plane
items.summary: In 1926, Nevanlinna (Acta Math. {\bf 48} (1926), no. 3-4, 367-391) proved that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ CM in the complex plane, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3,$ $a_4$ are four distinct complex values in the extended complex plane, then $f$ is a Möbius transformation of $g$, two of the shared values, say $a_1$ and $a_2$, are Picard exceptional values, and the cross ratio $\left(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4\right)=-1.$ Later on, Gundersen (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. {\bf 277} (1983), no. 2, 545-567. Correction: {\bf 304} (1987), 847-850) proved that if two non-constant meromorphic functions share two values CM and share two other values IM, then the functions share all four values CM. In 1992, Gundersen (Complex Var. Elliptic Equ. {\bf 20} (1992), no. 1-4, 99-106) proposed the following famous question: if two non-constant meromorphic functions share three distinct values IM and share a fourth value CM, then do the functions necessarily share all four values CM? This question is a long-standing question in the studies of the Nevanlinna's value distribution theory of meromorphic functions, and has not been completely resolved by now. In this paper, we completely resolve the question, and prove that if two distinct and non-constant meromorphic functions $f$ and $g$ share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ IM and $\infty$ CM, where $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ are three distinct and finite complex values in the complex plane, then $f$ and $g$ also share $a_1,$ $a_2,$ $a_3$ CM.

items.title: Unlikely intersections in Shimura varieties and beyond: a survey
items.summary: The aim of this note is to provide a concise introduction to so-called problems of unlikely intersections for (pure) Shimura varieties and to review the current state-of-the-art. In the process, we will touch upon more general settings and some of the results in those contexts.

items.title: Oort's conjecture on automorphisms of generic supersingular abelian varieties
items.summary: We prove Oort's conjecture that generically on the supersingular locus of the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of genus g and in characteristic p, the automorphism group of the universal principally polarized abelian variety consists only of $\pm 1$, unless g=2, 3 or 4 and p=2. On the way, we provide an explicit description of the a=1-locus in the Rapoport-Zink space of principally polarized supersingular p-divisible groups of any dimension g. We also prove analogous results for generic automorphism groups on moduli spaces of supersingular p-divisible groups with and without polarization.

items.title: Exclusion vs Noncolliding Dynamics in Markov Processes
items.summary: Let $(ξ_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a continuous-time Markov process taking values in a countable state space $E$. We consider $k$ copies of $ξ$ started from distinct positions, and write $X = (X_t)_{t \geq 0}$ for the resulting process of configurations in $E^k$. We compare two forms of interaction between the particles: the first is conditioning the particles to never collide (noncolliding dynamics), and the second is simply switching off any jumps that would cause two particles to occupy the same position (exclusion dynamics). We show under mild conditions on the tail probabilities of the collision time that the dynamics are related by an explicit exponential martingale change of measure of one another. This generalises a recent result in the integrable probability literature relating TASEP on the ring to asymmetric walkers conditioned to never collide.

items.title: Determination of the unbounded potential of the Robin Laplacian from fixed-time boundary measurements of time-fractional diffusion-wave equations
items.summary: We consider the time-fractional diffusion-wave equation $\partial_t^ρu - Δu + q u = 0$ in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \RR^n$, $n \geq 3$, where $\partial_t^ρ$ is the Caputo derivative of arbitrary order $ρ\in (0,2)$. This framework covers in a unified way the sub-diffusive case $ρ\in (0,1)$, the classical heat equation $ρ= 1$, and the super-diffusive case $ρ\in (1,2)$. The real-valued potential $q$ is only assumed to lie in $L^{n/2}(Ω)$, and the equation is endowed with zero initial conditions and a non-homogeneous Robin boundary condition, whose coefficient is allowed to be unbounded as well. The boundary excitations are supported in an arbitrary open subset $Γ_0$ of the boundary, and the trace of the solution is measured, at one fixed time, on another open subset $Γ_1$. We prove that the corresponding Robin-to-Dirichlet map uniquely determines the boundary spectral data of the underlying Robin Laplacian on $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$, provided that $Γ_0$ and $Γ_1$ overlap. When $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$ is the whole boundary, we deduce that $q$ is uniquely determined by this map in every dimension $n \geq 3$, the critical case $q \in L^{3/2}(Ω)$ in dimension three being included. The proof combines analytic continuation in the time variable, the Laplace transform and an identification of the poles and residues of meromorphic functions. The potential is then recovered from the boundary spectral data through an elliptic Robin-to-Dirichlet map, an integral identity, and complex geometric optics solutions.

items.title: Quasi-orthogonality is a geometric property
items.summary: Quasi-orthogonality is one of the key ingredients for proofs of optimal convergence rates for adaptive mesh refinement methods (Carstensen, Feischl, Page, and Praetorius, arXiv:1312.1171). The work of Feischl (arXiv:2008.12198) proposed a relaxed quasi-orthogonality that follows directly from the inf-sup stability of the underlying problem discretization. The proof uses an intricate connection to the stability of $LU$-factorization of matrices. Recently, Gantumur (arXiv:2609.16265) presented a vastly simplified argument based solely on Hilbert space arguments. Building on this idea, we show that quasi-orthogonality is a purely geometric property of a set of points. This property is checked for a large class of Petrov-Galerkin methods for monotone, non-linear equations.

items.title: Gradient Regularized Newton Boosting Trees with Global Convergence
items.summary: Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDTs) dominate tabular machine learning, with modern implementations like XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost being based on Newton boosting: a second-order descent step in the space of decision trees. Despite its empirical success, the global convergence of Newton boosting is poorly understood compared to first-order boosting. In this paper, we introduce Restricted Newton Descent, a framework for convex optimization with Newton's method on Hilbert spaces with inexact iterates, based on the concepts of cosine angle and weak gradient edge. Within this framework, we recover Newton boosting with GBDTs and classical finite-dimensional theory as special cases. We first prove that vanilla Newton boosting achieves a linear rate of convergence for smooth, strongly convex losses that satisfy a Hessian-dominance condition. To handle general convex losses with Lipschitz Hessians, we extend a recent gradient regularized Newton scheme to the restricted weak learner setting, establishing the first global $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{k^2})$ convergence rate for second-order GBDTs. This scheme minimally modifies the classical algorithm by introducing an adaptive $\ell_2$-regularization term proportional to the square root of the gradient norm at each iteration. In numerical experiments, we show that this scheme converges while vanilla Newton boosting may diverge.

items.title: Newtonian Dynamics in Metric Spaces
items.summary: We develop a variational framework for second-order, frictionless (Newtonian) dynamics in metric spaces, extending the metric theory of curves of maximal slope from gradient flows to evolutions with inertia. The construction rests on three pillars, mirroring the first-order theory. First, we introduce a class of second-order absolutely continuous curves, characterized by a geometric--variational inequality on families of tangent geodesics, and define a metric notion of acceleration. Second, we define curves of Newtonian motion as the curves achieving equality in an energy inequality involving an upper gradient--Hessian pair, which in Hilbert spaces is equivalent to Newton's equation $\ddotγ= -\nabla E(γ)$. Third, we propose a two-step predictor--corrector minimizing movement scheme and show that its discrete interpolants satisfy approximate versions of these inequalities. Under extendability and interceptor conditions on geodesics---which are satisfied, for instance, by geodesically uniformly complete, locally compact spaces with curvature bounded below---and under suitable regularity assumptions on the energy, we prove that the scheme converges, up to subsequences, to a curve of Newtonian motion. As an illustration, we recover the linear wave equation as a curve of Newtonian motion driven by the Dirichlet energy. This paper is complemented by the companion paper [Fornasier, Klemenc, Scagliotti, "A Lions Lift Framework for Gradient and Newtonian Evolutions in Wasserstein spaces"], which specifies and adapts the results to the Wasserstein metric space $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ through Lions lift, which explains Vlasov equations as Newtonian flows on spaces of probability measures.

items.title: A marking graph for finite-type Artin groups
items.summary: Clean markings on surfaces were a key component in Masur and Minsky's hierarchy machinery, which proved to be a powerful tool in the study of mapping class groups. We construct a marking graph for irreducible finite-type Artin groups which is quasi-isometric to the group modulo its center, i.e., an element of $A_Γ/Z(A_Γ)$ is determined up to finite error by its action on one of our markings. To construct this graph, we construct suitable collections of transverse parabolic subgroups which extend the maximal simplices of the complex of irreducible parabolic subgroups to analogues of clean markings, and we define natural analogues of elementary moves.

items.title: Inter-Categorical Subobject Analysis
items.summary: We introduce a systematic way to use the subobject functor on any category to set up a framework for generalized topological and measure-theoretic notions and inferences. Concretely, we develop two connected calculi: 1. a fourfold calculus derived from notions of smallness and density that generalizes, among other things, topological density and measure-theoretic negligibility, 2. a twofold calculus that generalizes topological and measure-theoretic inference procedures. The resulting theory is distinguished in that it is inter-categorical in character: its definitions can be applied not just to describe smallness and density of subobjects in any category and classify morphisms by how they handle them, but also functors and natural transformations by how they transform them, somewhat like the theory of limits but with a simple and intuitive conceptual meaning that applies to each incarnation. We provide examples of these notions from many areas of mathematics and outline their unfolding throughout category theory as we add assumptions that bring them closer to classical settings, which we complete by generalizing the topological duality of open and closed subsets and outlining a possible framework for a categorical measure theory. Central to this interaction is the subobject 2-functor and the 2-category of upward-bounded preorders, so in the last part of the text we provide a study of their function. Concretely we derive representation theorems for this 2-functor and 2-category and a conjecture about how to generalize these theorems to n-categories.

items.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
items.summary: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.

items.title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
